Sports.title: Revealed: Shocking food and drink prices at European Championships in Birmingham - with a pork roll costing £18.50 - as Stan Collymore hits out at bosses for pricing fans out
Sports.content:
Revealed: Shocking food and drink prices at European Championships in Birmingham - with a pork roll costing £18.50 - as Stan Collymore hits out at bosses for pricing fans out

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The European Athletics Championships have come under fire with fans being 'gouged' with 'disgusting' ticket and refreshment prices in Birmingham.

Star names such as Keely Hodgkinson, Katarina Johnson-Thompson, Dina Asher-Smith and Amy Hunt are competing in the first Championships to be held on these shores.

But seats are being flogged for up to £150 while a barbecue pork roll costs a piggish £18.50 at the Alexander Stadium.

Ticket prices are decided by European Athletics in collaboration with the Local Organising Committee.

The fees have been met with half-empty stands, with one supporter branding it a 'disgrace'.

Even former England footballer Stan Collymore has come out of the woodwork to criticise the pricing, writing on X: 'No wonder crowds yesterday were poor. Woeful optics.

'£18+ for a pork roll, £150 for a Cat A ticket. Could have got a £20 ticket for this morning's session but how many can go on a Tuesday in the school holidays?

The European Athletics Championships have seen tickets priced up to £150 - and have struggled to get bums on seats

The likes of Keely Hodgkinson (pictured), Katarina Johnson-Thompson, Dina Asher-Smith and Amy Hunt are competing

'Weather is amazing and the sport needs as many eyeballs as possible so kids for a quid!!

'£150/£100/£70 for the three categories at the weekend is aimed at who? Not families and kids who may want to be athletes!'

It's not just fans being priced out - athletes' families and friends are struggling to meet the costs too.

Athletes are not being given any complementary tickets for the events, but UK Athletics are not offering any discounts on this occasion.

At the 2024 Paris Olympics, athletes were given at least one free ticket and that is the case at the majority of major championships.

One anonymous athlete told The Times: 'They could have even offered a discounted rate, so it is a little bit of a surprise, a bit of a shame. It’s a home championships, it would be good to have more family and friends there but it’s sort of the hands we’ve been dealt really.'

Another said: 'We thought it was maybe a mistake at first.'

The extortionate food and drink prices include £15 for a bratwurst dog, £12 for barbecue loaded fries, and £3.95 for a bottle of water.

An X user wrote: 'Sorry but this is disgusting and a sure-fire way to turn people off a sport that gets only a couple of opportunities to show itself off each year. European Athletics Championships organisers in Birmingham need to be called out for this price gouging.'

Another said: 'Such a shame to see so many empty seats. Have watched those temporary stands go up in recent weeks, and yet so few people attending.'

One said: 'I was there. Half-empty stands were a disgrace. They knew ticket sales were dire, so where was the dynamic pricing model to drop prices, supported by marketing? And where was the back-up of giving tickets to youngsters in athletics clubs and other sports clubs? Embarrassing.'

Another replied to Collymore's post, saying: 'That's a joke. Country is on its knees as it is, how are they getting away with charging those prices expecting to attract families etc.? Ridiculous!'

Organisers said: 'Birmingham 2026 is delighted with ticket sales for the championships, which have far surpassed our targets.

'Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening sessions are approaching sell-out, with several other sessions close to capacity.

'There are still opportunities to be part of the championships at incredibly good value, including the ‘Mondo’ £6.31 children’s ticket for Friday morning - named in honour of his world record - while a family of four can attend for as little as £30.'

The European Athletics Championships are taking place from August 10 to 16, with Great Britain putting out a team of 96 competitors.

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Chelsea and Man United with Arsenal looking to sell after £75m Bruno Guimaraes capture
Sports.content:
Arsenal midfielder Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both Chelsea and Manchester United following the Gunners' capture of Bruno Guimaraes.

The 19-year-old signed a new deal last year following his breakout season, but after limited minutes in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign, there is belief the champions may be willing to move the Hale End product on.

There has been fresh contact with both the Blues and United, among other Premier League clubs, who are assessing whether to make a move for the versatile player.

Lewis-Skelly's minutes at Arsenal could be further limited in the upcoming season, with Guimaraes completing a £75million move from Newcastle last week.

Chelsea are understood to have long held an interest in Lewis-Skelly, but it is unclear whether they will put down an offer.

The academy product only managed 19 starts in all competitions last season, with Arteta giving him a rebirth in the middle of the park toward the end of the campaign, which led to a start in the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both Chelsea and Manchester United

Chelsea and United could both test Arsenal's resolve with a high enough offer for Lewis-Skelly

But with the Brazilian now expected to leapfrog Lewis-Skelly in the midfield pecking order, and opportunities already limited at left-back, there is a feeling that a move could be on the cards.

Guimaraes has signed a four-year deal with the option of a further 12 months. He adds serious talent and depth to Arsenal's midfield, which already contains names such as Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

A move to Chelsea would also see Lewis-Skelly face competition for minutes, with the Blues boasting a contingent of Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez – who has been linked with a move away – Romeo Lavia, Dario Essugo, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with new boss Xabi Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light.

The Blues have already made a series of statements in the transfer market, with Maxence Lacroix joining from Crystal Palace. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Teenager Lewis-Skelly has already made 75 senior appearances for Arsenal, securing a Premier League winner's medal last campaign.

He predominantly started his career at left-back, making a name for himself in Arsenal's Champions League quarter-final demolition of Real Madrid in 2025, but has since returned to his preferred position in central midfield.

The youngster has started every pre-season game for Arsenal, of which they have lost two, but is expected to be moved in place of Rice and Guimaraes once they return to action.

Sports.title: Defiant James McClean turns up for training at Derry City after poppy protestor's hometown club tried to rip up his contract
Sports.content:
James McClean rocked up for training at Derry City on Tuesday morning - despite the Northern Irish club reportedly trying to rip up his contract.

The 37-year-old rolled up in a black Range Rover despite a report in the Irish Independent claiming that Derry want to cancel his deal due to his supposed lack of 'physical capacity'.

Asked by reporters whether he was still a player with the club, McClean simply replied: 'Clearly.'

He was all smiles as he posed for photographs with young fans after the team's open training session.

McClean signed for his hometown club at the start of the 2026 season and has two years left on his deal, but has only started 12 of their 27 league games after leaving Wrexham.

The club reportedly claim that he is unable to fulfil his contract's terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

However the star - who has regularly made headlines for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations - is expected to insist that a contract cannot be cancelled unilaterally and that an independent physician must determine his fitness.

James McClean in Derry City training gear on Brandywell pitch meeting young fans at an open training session #jamesmcclean @UTVNews pic.twitter.com/Jd4jiqYrx1 — Gareth Wilkinson (@Gwilkinson_utv) August 11, 2026

WATCH. James McClean arrives at Brandywell Stadium for training amid reports Derry City has terminated his contract pic.twitter.com/db454kWy7U — Simon Collins (@SimonCollins82) August 11, 2026

James McClean has turned up for Derry City training despite them reportedly trying to rip up his contract

Derry sit sixth out of 10 teams in the League of Ireland Premier Division, a disappointing campaign after finishing runners-up in 2023 and 2025.

In June, McClean hinted at his unhappiness following his return home after a 15-year spell in English football.

'Family (are) enjoying being home – probably not so much myself, if I’m being honest,' McClean said during a punditry appearance on RTE.

'You know, you have a lot of conversations on the phone, and then you come home and you quickly realise that what you hear on the phone is not what you see in reality.

'There’s a lot of factors that’s contributed to that, but we’ll leave them for another day.'

McClean has previously spoken out about his reasons for not wearing the poppy, a decision he first made while playing for Sunderland in 2012. He maintained that stance throughout his career in England, despite being regularly targeted with abuse.

'The poppy which originally stood for World War 1 and 2 has now been adopted into honouring and remembering British soldiers that have served in all conflicts throughout the world including those who opened fire and murdered 14 innocent civilians on Bloody Sunday Jan 1972, in my home city, as well many other brutal crimes throughout Ireland,' McClean said in 2024.

'That is why I never have and never will wear a poppy. If the poppy’s sole purpose was to honour World War 1 and 2 then I would have no issue wearing it, but that’s not the case.

McClean has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations

'I respect those who do as I am fully aware we have different beliefs and upbringings, I would never force my beliefs on others, I’m not naive or stupid enough to expect the matter to be reciprocated, especially as the poppy is forced now on everyone in the UK and god forbid someone doesn’t wear it, the abuse they have to endure. The irony of all of this is that the poppy originally stood to honour those who fought for the right of freedom in both World Wars.

'Some people, no matter what, will not educate themselves or want to educate themselves, so to those who throw abuse about (matters they know nothing about), with insults like ‘hates our country’ – well I don’t. Some of my best relationships I’ve made through the years are with people born and raised in England and have completely different beliefs to me ... One thing I never have and never will do, is bend the knee to compromise my convictions.'

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland whom he represented in the Under 21s, said he had received 'death threats' for his stance over the poppy.

Last October, speaking during an episode of Virgin Media's Living with Lucy, he told presenter Lucy Kennedy how his family feared he would be shot while away on international duty after he first refused to wear a poppy on his shirt in 2012.

'I was getting death threats, people were saying I should be shot,' he said. 'I was getting bullets in the post, bullets sent to the club.

'That night, I met up with Ireland. The club had received threats that basically I was going to be shot. The game was on TV. I was going to be shot, this and that. (My wife, Erin) is back up in Newcastle, she’s panicking, she’s s*****g herself. They had to put security outside my hotel room door the whole night.

'Then, obviously, we’re playing the game, Erin’s watching the game, she’s panicking, she’s thinking, "He’s going to be shot on TV". Thankfully, nothing happened or nothing ever has happened.'

He added: 'I was getting death threats, people were saying he should be shot and dragged across the Cenotaph.

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland, said he has received 'death threats' for his poppy stance

'I could have easily just said, "I'll wear a poppy," and sold myself out and be known for my football or "I'll not wear a poppy" and be known as that but I've stayed true to myself.

'Six or seven people from the Creggan estate (where he grew up) died on Bloody Sunday that day so for me to wear a poppy in support of the people who carried out those atrocities...

'It frustrates me how people can’t see that. How is it even a debate of why I should wear the poppy?'

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton complete rare swap deal as Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil trade places - after Eagles held clear-the-air talks with star's girlfriend
Sports.content:
Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil have completed their respective swaps to Everton and Crystal Palace and signed four year contracts.

Johnson will join David Moyes' side, eight months after Palace signed him from Tottenham for a then club record fee of £35million, while McNeil will move from Merseyside to South London.

McNeil had been set to join the Eagles on Deadline Day in the winter and underwent his medical, but a deal that involved an initial loan with a £20m obligation to buy collapsed at the last minute.

That led to a furious reaction from Megan Sharpley, girlfriend of McNeil, who took to Instagram in a lengthy series of stories to hit out at what went on, including accusing Palace of messing with the winger's mental health.

The Eagles had submitted a deal sheet for McNeil's move, but then failed to complete the relevant paperwork in time. Everton sources said they fulfilled their part but Palace went quiet on finalising paperwork, effectively pulling out, and the transfer ran out of time.

Reports in The Times on Monday subsequently suggested that the club's co-owner and chairman Steve Parish held clear the air talks with Sharpley ahead of the transfer going through this time.

Brennan Johnson has completed a move to Everton from Crystal Palace in a rare swap deal

As part of the transfer, Dwight McNeil has moved the other way to link up with the Eagles after his transfer to the club on Deadline Day in the winter window collapsed at the last moment

In a searing statement following the collapse of the move, Sharpley described the 'cruelty' of the football world, saying that McNeil had been 'toyed with until the final minute' and subsequently 'left broken hearted with nothing but confusion'.

She said: 'Dwight, I've always been in awe of your job,' she began. 'The way you've committed most of your life to achieve what only the 0.1 per cent achieve.

'I know you love your job, the sport and you know how lucky you are to do what most people only dream of.

'We appreciate our lives, how fortunate we are, and the millions of football fans that keep the game alive and ultimately keep you in a job you adore. You've sacrificed a lot and most people don't have much of an idea of the difficult hardships you've suffered and dealt with in your personal life. And we crack on, that's who we are, we appreciate how blessed our lives are.

'But the world doesn't seem to accept that someone as fortunate as you is allowed to suffer hardships and feel sad. But you're a human, a beautiful incredible 26-year-old human being. And no matter about money or the success you've worked so hard to achieve, you are allowed to feel.

'Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you.'

Sharpley continued: 'To have something promised to you, to have been dragged along on an emotional rollercoaster, and to be toyed with until the final minute.

'To have 4-and-a-half-years of your life promised to you, traveling, medicals, agreements made... promises made. To have prepared to move your entire life, our life 100 of miles away in the space of a few hours.

'For it to be torn away from you at the last second, with absolutely no explanation. Going from everything - to radio silence, no phone call, no communication and be left, broken hearted with nothing but confusion, has hurt more than I can say.

'I sit with you, knowing in my heart and deep down into my soul that you will bounce back from this. I am your biggest supporter. And I know you will overcome this with a fire in your belly and a motivation that no one can stop. I have already seen it tonight, even whilst you're facing the lowest point of your career.'

McNeil's girlfriend Megan Sharpley hit out at the 'cruel' world of football after that move collapsed

After a lengthy series of Instagram stories from Sharpley, McNeil also spoke on the matter

Sharpley reaffirmed her support for her partner and revealed he had been left in tears by the collapse of the transfer.

'We live in a world where everyone is aware how big of a problem mental health is,' she added. 'So in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money, that it's okay to mess and toy with their mental health and that's just 'part of the job'?

'No matter of money, we all deserve to be treated with respect, kindness and fairly. So I really question the industry tonight. I only hope there's more done in the future to protect people from situations like what I've witnessed tonight.

'Football is brutal and yes, it's the nature of the beast, but messing with human beings feelings and emotions shouldn't be acceptable. People only see one side on the media, you don't see the tears, the emotion and the distress I've seen tonight.

'Dwight, to the present, and the future. Every single thing happens for a reason, I will always believe what is meant for you will find you, and with your hard work and determination I'll never doubt only the best will come your way, and I'm so excited to see what you can achieve...

'So here's to carrying on being an Everton player. The support we've had from this club, especially during my illness, has meant a lot on our journey, so let's keep grinding, keep working and grafting for this badge. Let's keep going Dwight, show them who you are. I'm right by your side.'

The emotional post from Sharpley referenced her own illness when she was diagnosed with a large, serious tumour on her ovary and was forced to undergo urgent open surgery in December 2023. McNeil was praised for his unwavering support at the time.

The winger, who has played 128 times for Everton since joining from Burnley in 2022, also weighed in on the situation in regards to his failed move.

Sharing the final story from his partner, McNeil added: 'Whilst even now I'm still left in the dark. What I do know, and have been supported with, I am an Everton player. I will use this as motivation.

'I love you moo, I couldn't thank you enough for all of your love and support.'

Meanwhile, after completing his move to Merseyside, Johnson told evertontv: ‘I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

'There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.'

He becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes’ squad after Merlin Rohl’s loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

McNeil has signed his four-year contract with Palace and said: 'The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.'

Sports.title: Paul Scholes urges Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for 'nutcase' Cristian Romero - despite calling him 'an absolute clown' who 'does stupid things'
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes urges Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for 'nutcase' Cristian Romero - despite calling him 'an absolute clown' who 'does stupid things'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has urged his former club to gazump Atletico Madrid's £34million move for Cristian Romero, despite branding the Tottenham captain a 'nutcase' and 'absolute clown' in his sales pitch.

The Argentina defender, 28, is expected to leave Spurs this summer after being given the green light to join LaLiga heavyweights Atletico Madrid, who are deep in talks with the north London outfit and only a few million apart in negotiations.

Meanwhile, the Red Devils are eagerly exploring options to bolster Michael Carrick's squad ahead of the new campaign, which will see United compete in the Champions League after finishing third in the Premier League last season.

Scholes, who has previously criticised Romero's rash and ill-disciplined approach to defending at Spurs, has surprisingly called for United to hijack Atletico's pursuit.

'This is one you might laugh at. Cristian Romero from Tottenham,' he said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast while discussing potential transfer targets for United.

'I know it might sound stupid, but I just think... I like him. I think he's a nutcase. He's a very good defender that does some stupid things. He is an absolute clown.

Paul Scholes has urged Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for Cristian Romero

Scholes branded the defender a 'nutcase' but still thinks he would bring something to United

'But I think if someone could get hold of him, like Michael Carrick, who is very calm and relaxed, he might be able to [help him].

'He seems like a bit of a cult hero defender, really. I know it might sound strange, but I think the fans at Old Trafford would like him.

'There's a bit of something about him. He's won the Europa League with Spurs, he's won a World Cup, two Copa Americas. There's definitely something about him and he's cheap, £30-40million.'

Carrick has a string of defensive options at centre-half heading into the season, with Harry Maguire, Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt, Ayden Heaven and Romero's international team-mate Lisandro Martinez among those who operate at the heart of defence.

Scholes believes, despite the options available, that United need to bolster that department in particular if they plan to kick on in the future.

'I think centre-half is probably the biggest [area that needs addressing],' he added. 'You need to have centre-halves that are reliable for the Premier League. You’d like to have them [fit enough to play] in most games.

'Harry Maguire not so much, but Martinez picks up a lot of injuries. They’ve got the young lad Ayden Heaven, who I think is a really bright prospect, but he’s still going to make mistakes. He’s young.

'Centre-half is a position they need to address if they are going to be challenging towards the top end [of the league].'

Manchester United's first test in the Premier League is a trip to newly-promoted Hull City on Saturday, August 22.

Sports.title: Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - with Chelsea set for a windfall -as Napoli offer £2m loan fee for Blues defender Benoit Badiashile, and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - with Chelsea set for a windfall -as Napoli offer £2m loan fee for Blues defender Benoit Badiashile, and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

World Cup star joins Forest

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon.

The 22-year-old centre-back has signed a four-year deal with an option for another year.

Diomande said: 'It is a historic club, and it motivates me to join such a club. I believe we can achieve very good things this season and I am looking forward to meeting the players and head coach.

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon

'I will give my best and all I can to help the team. I cannot wait to meet the supporters at the City Ground and together we can have a good season.'

Forest still want to add a right-back, midfielder and striker.

Patterson completes Wrexham medical

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move to Wrexham.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed yesterday, the 26-year-old has agreed terms on a four-year deal with the Championship club.

Patterson is finalising the paperwork on his contract.

Wrexham are also in talks to sign Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt in a £4.5m deal.

Hull get their Nobel prize

Hull City have finally agreed their protracted negotiations for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

The centre back is heading over for his medical after the clubs settled on a £21million fee plus 12.5per cent sell-on clause, while his former club Real Betis receive 20 percent as part of their sell-on.

The 21-year-old Senegal international can play at centre back and left-back.

Fulham snap up Southampton's Charles

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons.

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year contract, tying him to Craven Cottage until June 2031, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months.

Southampton also retain a 20percent sell-on.

Speaking to FFCtv, Charles, who will wear the number 19 shirt, said: 'It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege.

'I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.

'I’m buzzing to finally get it over the line. The club has got a really good foundation, from the bottom to the top really.'

Palace and Everton complete rare swap deal

Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil have completed their respective swaps to Everton and Crystal Palace and signed four year contracts.

Johnson, who only joined Palace from Tottenham in January for £35m, told evertontv: ‘I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

Brennan Johnson has completed a move to Everton from Crystal Palace in a rare swap deal

As part of the transfer, Dwight McNeil has moved the other way to link up with the Eagles after his transfer to the club on Deadline Day in the winter window collapsed at the last moment

'There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

He becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes’ squad after Merlin Rohl’s loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

Meanwhile, McNeil has signed his four-year contract with Palace and said: 'The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.'

Lukaku agrees Turkey move

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli.

The Belgium international has agreed a two year contract worth around £8.6m a season and has already passed his medical.

The deal includes further add ons based on performances.

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli

Chelsea are understood to have inserted a 40percent sell-on clause when they sold Lukaku for a knockdown £26m to Napoli two years ago.

He scored 14 goals in his first season but injury and the arrival of Rasmus Hojlund from Manchester United restricted him to just seven games last year.

Liverpool starlet wanted in Portugal

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move.

The 18-year-old who has joined the club from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal has stood out for the first team in pre-season friendlies.

But despite the promise he has shown, and Liverpool's dearth of defensive cover, post-Brexit rules mean Austria youth international Ndukwe doesn't have enough points to obtain a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) to obtain a work visa.

He will start against Como in their last friendly but is unable to play a competitive match for the Anfield club.

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move

Now clubs from Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have been calling to take the 6ft 6ins centre back on loan but there is a sense Portugal may be his preferred destination.

After playing alongside him, captain Virgil van Dijk said: 'Big talent, big guy and he wants to learn. I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him, it is just progressing. I know he has to go on loan I think so let's see where he ends up.'

Napoli still in the hunt for Badiashile

Napoli have offered a £2m loan fee for Chelsea's £30million-rated centre-back Benoit Badiashile with obligation to buy.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs and the player's representatives to try and find a full agreement.

Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah to Como and are also looking to sell Axel Disasi who has had interest from Crystal Palace and West Ham.

Napoli are continuing talks to sign Chelsea's £30m-rated centre-back Beniot Badiashile (right)

Mamadou Sarr, who suffered an injury at the weekend, is likely to go on loan to a Premier League side.

Keeper Filip Jorgensen has completed his move to Strasbourg on loan.

Wigan Athletic are closing in on their loan move for Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh while Portsmouth want 17-year-old Chelsea winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen on loan.

Napoli remain keen on Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus also as talks continue. Arsenal want £20m for the Brazilian.

Villa defender wanted in Belgium

Aston Villa right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic is a target for Rangers along with Hugo Siquet of Bruges.

Nedeljkovic has had interest from a number of clubs including Osasuna but Rangers are exploring a £4million deal with initial loan for the Serbia international.

The 20-year-old had a spell with RB Leipzig last season.

Burnley after new keeper

Burnley are showing interest in OH Leuven goalkeeper Tobe Leysen.

The 24-year-old former Belgium U21 international has one year left on contract so Leuven are willing to listen to offers.

Sports.title: The 12 biggest breakout talents in world rugby pushing to be World Cup bolters: England's Northampton duo, the Springbok fly-half who took on Beauden Barrett, Finn Russell's Scotland successor and Australia's 'generational talent'
Sports.content:
The 12 biggest breakout talents in world rugby pushing to be World Cup bolters: England's Northampton duo, the Springbok fly-half who took on Beauden Barrett, Finn Russell's Scotland successor and Australia's 'generational talent'

Unlock more of the best of our rugby coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

The countdown is on to the biggest showpiece in rugby.

With a little over 12 months until the 2027 World Cup, Test sides will spend the next year finessing their squads before heading to Australia.

While the next World Cup might arrive too soon for some of the best young talents across the globe, there will undoubtedly be a bolter or two that will come to the fore.

Here, Daily Mail Sport’s ALEX BYWATER looks at 12 stars of the next generation ready to make a name for themselves.

Yaqeen Ahmed

Age: 20, Country: South Africa, Club: Stormers Position: Fly-half

South Africa are hoping to become the first team to win three World Cups in a row, and already have perhaps the most exciting young fly-half in world rugby in Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

And the bad news for their rivals is they already have another dazzling No10 coming through the youth ranks, in No10 Ahmed.

He was at the centre of his country’s Under-20 World Cup win in Georgia this summer and despite his young age, has already developed a reputation as a playmaker with an all-round game.

Ahmed played for his club side Stormers against New Zealand last weekend, going up against the great Beauden Barrett, which no doubt would have aided his already impressive development even further.

Yaqeen Ahmed has already had a shot at the All Blacks, as part of their ongoing tour of South Africa while playing for the Stormers

Lucas Friday

Age: 20, Country: England, Club: Harlequins Position: Scrum-half

As Steve Borthwick attempts to turn England into World Cup contenders, there are a few exciting prospects he can call upon.

Friday, the son of former England sevens coach Mike, is a very promising scrum-half who has become a regular in senior matchday squads for Harlequins.

He has played for England’s Under 20s side for three years, winning the Junior World Cup when he had just turned 18. Now over a serious knee injury, Friday has expert distribution and a desire to play the game quickly.

Tom Howe

Age: 18, Country: Wales, Club: Cardiff Position: Hooker

A little over a year ago, I was walking my dog in Cardiff when I bumped into a former contact. ‘Remember this name,’ he told me. ‘It’s Tom Howe. He’s going to be a Wales international.’ Most people you speak to in Welsh rugby seem to be of the same opinion.

At a dark time for the country’s national game, Howe is a player of real promise. He’s already trained with Cardiff’s senior side and would have been picked by Wales’ Under 20s earlier were it not for age restrictions.

Hookers tend to take a while to develop, but Howe has all the raw potential, so don’t be surprised if he steps up quickly.

Treyvon Pritchard

Age: 19, Country: Australia, Club: Queensland Reds Position: Utility back

Pritchard lit up Super Rugby in his debut season with the Reds. He can play anywhere across the back line and has been described as a ‘generational talent’ by Rugby Australia chief executive Phil Waugh.

Such is his ability, he quickly became a target for rugby league sides in his homeland, but he has committed to playing union on a new long-term deal – a significant boost for Les Kiss’s Wallabies.

His dazzling run for Australia’s Under 20s against France this summer is worth checking out, if you want a glimpse of his talents. His brother Kadin, 21, is some player too.

View this post on Instagram

Treyvon Pritchard lit up Super Rugby in his debut season with the Reds. He can play anywhere across the back line and has been described as a ‘generational talent’

Fergus Watson

Age: 21, Country: Scotland, Club: Glasgow Warriors Position: Wing

Scotland have been rightly criticised for not producing enough homegrown talent, but that looks like it might be changing.

Livingston-born Glasgow wing Watson has all the attributes to be a force in the modern game. At 6ft 3in and nearly 16st, he blends significant size with pace, as the likes of George North have done before him.

Watson marked his competitive Warriors debut in March with a try against Benetton. Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend has an ageing squad, so Watson might soon get a chance if he goes well in this season’s United Rugby Championship.

James Pater

Age: 19, Country: England, Club: Northampton Saints Position: Full-back

Pater made his senior Northampton debut at just 17 and is likely to have more opportunities with Saints this season after George Furbank’s move from the PREM Rugby champions to Harlequins.

He can play fly-half as well as at No15, but it's in the back field where he is likely to develop. Pater is still eligible to play for England Under 20s in the coming campaign, but looks ready for action at a higher level.

A talented all-round sportsman, Pater was in Cambridge United’s academy as a boy. He is rated highly at Northampton.

James Pater (right) made his senior Northampton debut at just 17 and is likely to have more opportunities with Saints this season after George Furbank’s move to Harlequins

Josh Neill

Age: 19, Country: Ireland, Club: Leinster Position: Flanker

Neill went viral when doing interviews on Ireland Under 20s duty due to his strong African accent. He has been poached by the Irish system from South Africa and has committed his future to both Leinster and the national team.

Given Leinster produce so much homegrown talent, the fact they have gone out of their way to move for Neill speaks volumes. He qualifies for Ireland through his grandparents.

At 6ft 4in, Neill is tall for a flanker. His grounding came at Rondebosch Boys’ High School, a traditional South African rugby nursery that has produced generations of elite players. Now, his future lies in Dublin.

Hugh Shields

Age: 18, Country: England, Club: Northampton Saints Position: Fly-half

Another promising Englishman at Northampton. Shields’ father, Paul, also represented Saints, as well as Ulster and Ireland. But his son has pursued a career with England, for whom he has played at all age-group levels.

Shields was England Under 20s' fly-half in Georgia earlier this summer and is still only 18. A promising game-manager and a strong kicker, Shields was arguably England’s standout performer in their Junior World Cup semi-final defeat by South Africa, as he put in a display that suggested he has the talent and drive to progress to the senior side.

The Northampton playmaker scored two tries against the Junior Springboks and also claimed 12 points with the boot in an impressive 22-point haul. He caught the eye again in the third-place play-off loss to New Zealand and will hope to maintain his upward trajectory.

Hugh Shields was England Under 20s' fly-half in Georgia earlier this summer and is still only 18

Jake Dalziel

Age: 17, Country: Scotland, Club: Newcastle Red Bulls Position: Fly-half

Even at his tender age, Dalziel is already viewed in many quarters as the long-term successor to Scotland and Bath No10 Finn Russell.

He is the son of Scotland forwards coach John, who was also a coach on the 2025 British & Irish Lions tour. Dalziel is regarded as one of the brightest talents Scotland has produced for many, many years.

He made his Scotland Under 20s breakthrough last season and has already signed for Newcastle Red Bulls, for whom Scotland head coach Townsend is a consultant, having also had interest from Bath. He is still only 17 so has time on his side, but his talent may demand he progresses very quickly.

Even at his tender age, Jake Dalziel is already viewed in many quarters as the long-term successor to Scotland and Bath No 10 Finn Russell

Lucas Andjisseramatchi

Age: 20, Country: France, Club: La Rochelle Position: Back-row

France is the only country currently capable of rivalling South Africa in terms of the quality of their talent production line.

Their junior side were beaten in the final of this summer’s World Cup by the Springboks, with La Rochelle’s Andjisseramatchi as captain. He had previously helped France win the junior Six Nations.

A charismatic character off the field, on it Andjisseramatchi sets the tone with his tireless work rate. He's not afraid of scoring tries, either!

A charismatic character off the field, on it Lucas Andjisseramatchi sets the tone with his tireless work rate

Ollie Blyth-Lafferty

Age: 20, Country: Scotland, Club: Edinburgh Position: Prop

Blyth-Lafferty made an impressive first start for Edinburgh in a European Champions Cup victory over Toulon last year and then signed his first professional contract with the club.

Described by age-group coach Kenny Murray as an 'exceptional prospect', Blyth-Lafferty props the scrum on the tighthead side, and captained his country at Under-20 level in a Junior World Cup warm-up with Ireland in the summer.

Cohen Norrie

Age: 19, Country: New Zealand, Club: Blues Position: Fly-half

Scotland-qualified Hurricanes fly-half Harry Godfrey is being marketed for a move to European rugby, clearing the way for Norrie to stake his claim as New Zealand's next great prospect.

With Beauden Barrett and Damian McKenzie both into their 30s, Cohen Norrie will have his sights set on being the next great All Black No10

He certainly filled that role for the Baby Blacks this summer, also showing his versatility by filling in at full-back.

He won the Auckland Emerging Player of the Year award this year and has starred for New Zealand's Under 20s. With Barrett and Damian McKenzie both into their 30s, Norrie will have his sights set on being the next great All Black No10.

Sports.title: Golfer hits staggering 411-yard hole-in-one and is so shocked he can't find the ball
Sports.content:
Golfer hits staggering 411-yard hole-in-one and is so shocked he can't find the ball

An incredible new national record could have been set by an amateur golfer who hit an incredible 411-yard shot, which has estimated odds of six million-to-one

View 4 Images Matt Vigurs hit an incredible 411 yards hole-in-one (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

A golfer has incredibly set what is thought to be Britain's longest hole-in-one shot, at an incredible 411 yards (376 metres).

‌



Matt Vigurs, from Droitwich in Worcestershire, narrowly missed out on setting a new Guinness World Record when he aced the third hole during a recent match, but he could be in store for a national record. The 32-year-old made the incredible shot during a recent league match at Great Barr Golf Club in Sandwell, near Birmingham.

‌



The golfer hit his driver off the tee but could not find his shot when he reached the green. After a few minutes searching, Matt decided to have a quick look in the hole and saw his ball.

‌



Golf star punished after fish eats his ball during round leaving pundits gobsmacked READ MORE :

View 4 Images The shot was hit at Great Barr Golf Club (Image: Google Maps / SWNS)

Matt said: "It was really surreal. I just froze to start with. The lads ran over and we all belly slammed and high fived. It was a moment I will never forget for sure. It was brilliant. I think we were all shocked. Typically, the ball wouldn't go that far. It is just unheard of to get a hole-in-one really let alone on a par-four."

The golfer revealed that his average drive is around 300 yards but the wind and hard ground helped him stretch out to 411 yards. The incredible shot however was just 36 yards (33 metres) short of all-time record of a 447 yards (408 metres) hole-in-one, set by Robert Mitera in Nebraska, USA.

‌



View 4 Images Matt hit the hole-in-one on his third (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

Despite this, England Golf - the national governing body for amateur golf - believe Matt could have achieved a national record, but this has not yet been confirmed. It is thought the golfer beat the previous national effort by three yards. Peter Vickerman aced the 408-yard par-four seventh hole at Littlestone Golf Club in Kent, in 2014.

Matt's hole-in-one - also known as an albatross - came in a scratch match at the Walsall golf club, playing with a friend against two others. The four-ball found three balls when they got to the green of the hole, named Twin Oaks - but Matt's was missing.

‌



They searched the bushes, around the fairway and over the back of the green but it was nowhere to be seen. On a whim, Matt, who plays off a handicap of +1, decided to check the hole and says his friends gave him strange looks for even checking.

View 4 Images Matt Vigurs after winning the Worcestershire County Championship (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

Matt said: "At that point I looked a bit silly, so I thought I might as well check the hole - and there it was, nestled in the bottom. I had to take two or three looks. I couldn't believe it. They didn't believe me till I pulled it out of the hole and we just went mad! It was so weird - I couldn't concentrate for the next hole!"

‌



Matt, who only returned to regular golf in February after eight years abroad, went on to win his match. Droitwich Golf Club as a result sealed promotion by winning the league on the same day.

The odds of getting an albatross - a score of three-under-par - are estimated to be odds of six million-to-one, according to England Golf. However, the odds of a hole-in-one from this distance even likely even slimmer.

Matt, who works as a product and training manager at McLaren, added: "We think it might be the longest which is quite cool actually. I think it might even be the longest in Europe. I have absolutely no chance of ever doing it again. It truly was a once in six-million shot."

Article continues below

The golfer, who started playing the sport aged 11, said he kept the ball and hopes his golf club might help him commemorate the achievement.

James Crampton, championships director at England Golf, said: "We hear of holes-in-one all the time, but a 411-yard one - it's the stuff of golfers' dreams! It sounds like Matt is in the purple patch of his golfing life - and you have to enjoy these moments."

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy U-turns on golf break after pointed message to PGA Tour chiefs
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy U-turns on golf break after pointed message to PGA Tour chiefs

Rory McIlroy has had a change of heart ahead of his return to action

View 3 Images Rory McIlroy is set to return to action for the first time since The Open (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Rory McIlroy has changed his tune on the FedEx Cup by entering the first leg of this year's Playoffs. The world number two was criticised 12 months ago for skipping the first FedEx Cup event, as it did not affect his position in the rankings and offered a chance to have a break ahead of the Ryder Cup.

‌



The FedEx Cup Playoffs is the end-of-season series for the PGA Tour. Throughout the regular season, players earn points based on their tournament finishes. When the regular season concludes in August, the top point earners qualify for a three-event playoff sequence that determines the overall season champion.

‌



The first Playoff event, the St Jude Championship, has a field of 70. For the second, the BMW Championship, it is whittled down to 50. Then, for the Tour Championship season decider, the field is made up of the top 30 players on the list.

‌



McIlroy goes into this year's Playoffs in 12th spot, with his place in the Tour Championship virtually assured even if he doesn't play in the first two events. As recently as last month's Open Championship, McIlroy said he was prepared to miss the opening Playoffs events and questioned the format in a pointed message to PGA Tour chiefs.

Rory McIlroy's caddie has earned astonishing amount of money in 2026 alone READ MORE :

Ahead of last year's Playoffs, the Starting Strokes format, which benefited the players higher up the leaderboard, was dropped. It saw the leader start on 10 under par, while the players 26th to 30th on the list began on level par.

McIlroy said at The Open: "I guess I'm just at a stage that I have other things that I prioritise. The PGA Tour is in a lot of flux at the minute, with a lot of their schedule and structure and everything like that.

‌



View 3 Images McIlroy has questioned the FedEx Cup format (Image: R&A via Getty Images)

"So, I think the change where it doesn't matter where you are in the top 30 going into the Tour Championship, it's like I just need to be in the top 30 going in there to have a chance to win a FedEx Cup.

"So why would I care about the first two? I sort of came to that decision last year, and I'm just sort of doing the same thing."

‌



However, McIlroy has performed a U-turn by entering the St Jude Championship after all. He will be joined by the likes of Scottie Scheffler, who topped the regular-season leaderboard and banked a £7.4million bonus as a result.

View 3 Images Scottie Scheffler is the man to beat heading into the FedEx Cup playoffs (Image: Getty Images)

This is the first time since 2021 that McIlroy will enter the first leg of the Playoffs outside the top 10 in the standings, but it would be foolish to write the Masters champion off.

Article continues below

In changes that may please McIlroy, the PGA Tour will introduce a two-tier structure from 2028. A new-look Tour Championship will be hosted at a "rotation of prestigious courses, many of which the PGA Tour would play for the first time," said the Tour.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer

Arsenal could have Newcastle United to thank for a summer transfer boost days after raiding St James' Park to sign Bruno Guimaraes

View 2 Images Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United for £75m but could recoup millions (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Arsenal could be set to recoup some of the £75m transfer fee they paid for Bruno Guimaraes just days later, thanks to a shrewd transfer clause included as part of Joe Willock's switch to Newcastle United. The Gunners negotiated a sell-on clause with the Magpies when Willock moved to St. James' Park back in 2021.

‌



The 26-year-old left the Emirates Stadium in a deal valued at £25million after an impressive loan spell with the Magpies, but his five-year stay in the North East may be coming to an end. Willock is now believed to be close to a £17.4m move to Turkish Super Lig outfit Besiktas, with Newcastle having turned down a £10m bid earlier this summer.

‌



Our sister title ChronicleLive reports Willock's representatives have travelled to Turkey to negotiate a move with Besiktas, reportedly reaching agreement on personal terms. The former Arsenal midfielder is entering the final 12 months of his contract at St. James' Park and Newcastle are keen to recoup a fee.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

That's positive news for the Gunners, who secured a sell-on clause rumoured to be around 20 per cent, though the precise percentage remains undisclosed. Arsenal spent £75m to take Guimaraes to north London and could bank millions from Willock's prospective move, recouping some of the money paid for the Brazilian.

Gunners fans got a first glimpse of the new midfield addition ahead of the Emirates Cup clash with Borussia Dortmund at the weekend. As for his former Magpies teammate, Willock has featured 168 times for Newcastle, netting 11 goals since his departure from the Gunners.

‌



He broke into the Arsenal first team in 2017 and memorably scored on his Premier League debut against Newcastle in April 2018. Willock racked up 78 appearances and registered 11 goals during four campaigns at the club.

View 2 Images Willock found a new home in the north east (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

The clause now ensures Mikel Arteta's side will profit financially. Arsenal are looking to bolster their squad ahead of their Premier League title defence, having already brought in Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Guimaraes.

‌



The additional funds will provide a welcome boost in their bid to secure further signings this summer, with the Gunners actively seeking a new left-winger.

Arsenal had been linked with moves for Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, however Chelsea swooped in to snap up the England international, while Real Madrid tied down the Brazilian star to fresh terms.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup fixture chaos as Chelsea embroiled in crazy eight-game domino effect
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup fixture chaos as Chelsea embroiled in crazy eight-game domino effect

Chelsea will take on Luton Town at Stamford Bridge in the second round of the Carabao Cup as Premier League clubs enter the competition

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso's Chelsea will take on Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup. (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

There could be a major fixture list shift following the second round Carabao Cup draw. The Premier League kicks off in just under two weeks, with Chelsea travelling to take on Fulham in the final fixture of the weekend on Monday, August 24 (8pm kick-off).

‌



The match is being played on the Monday night after being selected for live TV coverage on Sky Sports. But it is now set to impact a few other fixtures, with both Chelsea and Fulham in action in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

‌



Chelsea will face League One side Luton Town at Stamford Bridge on the week commencing August 24. Fulham, meanwhile, have been drawn at home against AFC Wimbledon.

‌



Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected READ MORE :

Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis SUING Crystal Palace over gun banner READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Typically, these matches are played on Tuesday or Wednesday evenings, but the Monday night clash between Chelsea and Fulham on the Premier League's opening weekend means that both fixtures are likely to be pushed back to Thursday, August 27.

With Chelsea's fixture against Brighton, and Fulham's clash against Sunderland the following weekend already confirmed for Sunday, this shouldn't present any issues. There is, however, another potential complication for schedulers to navigate.

‌



Policing constraints typically prevent Chelsea and Fulham from hosting matches on the same day. This will either need changes to existing regulations, or an alternative solution will need to be found by the EFL.

While both Chelsea and Fulham don't return to action until the following Sunday, the same cannot be said for their respective opponents. Both Luton and AFC Wimbledon are scheduled to fulfil League One commitments against Mansfield Town (A) and Wigan Athletic (H) on the Saturday, less than 48 hours after the potential Thursday night fixture.

View 2 Images Jack Wilshere's Luton will take on Chelsea in the second round of the Carabao Cup. (Image: Eddie Keogh/Getty Images)

‌



Clubs are generally granted a minimum of 72 hours' rest between fixtures, suggesting those matches are likely to be postponed by approximately 24 hours. Nevertheless, this will then create a domino effect on their midweek commitments.

All four sides are set to feature in league action on Tuesday, 1 September. Those encounters will consequently need to be rescheduled by 24 hours to the Wednesday evening to ensure the teams receive sufficient rest between the two fixtures, meaning up to eight games will need to be moved.

Sports.title: Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd
Sports.content:
Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd

Manchester United have Marcus Rashford back at the club after two loans away but a swap deal with Arsenal has been touted by a former player

Marcus Rashford speaks to the media during England's World Cup campaign

Former Arsenal defender Lee Dixon admits he'd swap Marcus Rashford for Myles Lewis-Skelly and believes Mikel Arteta would "be great" for the Manchester United frontman.

‌



The forward is back at Old Trafford after Barcelona opted against making his loan move permanent. It means he could appear for his boyhood club for the first time in more than 18 months and has just been handed a new squad number, 14, suggesting a first-team role is likely.

‌



Rashford has endured peaks and troughs during his United career but, when on form, is an impressive performer. Across his decade at the Red Devils he's scored six times against Arsenal.

‌



The Gunners themselves are in the market for reinforcements in the final third and, with Lewis-Skelly facing an uncertain future due to his standing in the pecking order, Dixon has suggested a swap would be a good move.

Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours READ MORE :

Man Utd decide on giving Marcus Rashford new shirt number in clear hint on future READ MORE :

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back with Man Utd after two loan spells away (Image: Richard Sellers/Allstar, Getty Images)

He told BestBettingSites: "Would I swap them (Myles Lewis Skelly and Marcus Rashford)? You know what, I probably would. And that's nothing against Myles Lewis-Skelly; it's about giving him the freedom to go and expand his game elsewhere.

‌



"With Marcus Rashford, he's a player who needs an arm around his shoulder, and Arteta would be great for him. Give him that love, give him the freedom to play on that left side, and yeah, I'd like to see him in an Arsenal shirt. I have my reservations about whether he's consistently a top-class player, but based on what Arsenal have in the squad now, he'd be a good addition."

United's frontline has been revamped since Rashford was frozen out by Ruben Amorim with Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko all ariving. Amad Diallo also continues to blossom.

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly is far from a guaranteed starter at Arsenal (Image: Getty)

‌



The 28-year-old has been linked with a permanent exit on numerous occasions, but is set to be re-integrated into the team during pre-season ahead of their Premier League opener.

At Arsenal, Lewis-Skelly recovered from a disappointing opening few months and ended up starting in the Champions League final. He only started five league games and was far more utilised in the Champions League by Arteta.

His versatility makes him an asset and United have been looking to bolster their ranks in midfield and at left-back - two positions that Lewis-Skelly can play.

Sports.title: Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours
Sports.content:
Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours

Bruno Fernandes has been a key player for Manchester United since joining the club in 2020 and a former team-mate has spoken about a classy gesture

View 3 Images Brandon Williams says ex-Manchester United colleague Bruno Fernandes still checks up on him (Image: Getty)

Brandon Williams says former Manchester United team-mate Bruno Fernandes still messages him and helps him get match tickets. Williams is currently without a club after leaving Hull City in February.

‌



Since 2023, Fernandes has been United's skipper and for all intents and purposes, the face of the club. But it's not just on the field where he is influential.

‌



Defender Williams, who joined the club's academy ranks at the age of seven, left United in 2024 after the expiration of his contract and has faced legal trouble in the years since. But the 25-year-old is still in contact with some of his former team-mates at Old Trafford and Fernandes in particular showed his class with a kind act.

‌



Williams told The Athletic how Fernandes still keeps in touch with him and arranges match tickets. He said: "That's why he's the captain, he's an unreal guy."

The left-back is presently a free agent. He worked his way through United's youth set-up before making his senior debut in 2019. That season, with Luke Shaw and Ashley Young battling fitness problems, he secured meaningful minutes and penned a fresh four-year contract in 2020.

‌



A loan switch to Norwich City in 2021 was followed by another temporary stint with Ipswich Town. While he failed to truly shine during these spells, his career trajectory shifted in 2023.

View 3 Images Williams played 51 times for United (Image: Getty)

Williams was charged and subsequently found guilty of dangerous driving and driving without third-party insurance following a traffic collision on the A34 near Wilmslow/Handforth.

Eyewitnesses described seeing him drive recklessly, tailgating, braking sharply and holding a balloon to his mouth, although prosecutors emphasised there was no proof he was legally impaired. He lost control and smashed into a Ford Fiesta at around 74mph before careering into the central reservation.

He originally denied the charges but admitted guilt in March 2025 and was sentenced in May to 14 months' imprisonment, suspended for two years, a three-year driving ban and an unpaid community work order of 180 hours. As Williams tries to rebuild his career, he claims that if he still fancies going to watch his boyhood club, Fernandes can lend a hand.

Williams revealed that he also remains in touch with fellow former team-mates Marcus Rashford and Harry Maguire. His United contract ran out in 2024 and following a short break, he penned a one-year deal with Hull last year.

Having been without a club since February, Williams has been training with League Two outfit Rotherham but remains uncertain whether he'll land a contract. Looking back on his career, he added: "I've only just started to look back and be like, 'I actually did something.' I actually played for United 51 times. It's something to be proud of.

"I know it's not going to be a quick process, I know I'm not going to be in the Premier League next year. I'm ready to climb the mountain and get back to the top of it."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola 'gives transfer green light' and star joins up with squad
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola 'gives transfer green light' and star joins up with squad

Liverpool are gearing up for the return of the Premier League with some pre-season fixtures at Anfield

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola has reportedly said 'yes' to Liverpool (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
