World.title: INEC impartiality, key to Nigeria’s survival in 2027 – PFN President, Bishop Oke
World.content:
Says government should come hard on religious extremists

By Dayo Johnson Akure

The National President of the Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria, PFN, Bishop Wale Oke, has warned that the integrity of the nation hangs in the balance of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, remaining unbiased ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Speaking with newsmen at the 38th annual convention of Agape Christian Ministries in Akure, Ondo State, the cleric also urged the Federal Government to “come down hard” on religious extremists bent on transforming Nigeria into a caliphate state.

On the impartiality of the electoral body, Bishop Oke stressed the need for an INEC free from political influence.

“INEC is a government functionary. It is not part of any political party. INEC is to regulate all political parties and to conduct elections, not to take sides with any,” he said.

“We are demanding that for the exercise of our civil rights, INEC does not partake in partisan politics. The integrity of Nigeria’s democracy hangs in the balance.”

Ahead of the 2027 elections, the PFN President advised politicians to avoid ethnic and religious biases and focus instead on competence.

“Politicians should not play the ethnic card in choosing who leads us. They should not play the religious card,” he said.

“If the presidential candidate is a Muslim, is it not fair to have the vice-presidential candidate as a Christian so that both faiths will be represented in the Villa? If the presidential candidate is a Christian, the vice president should be a Muslim to balance it.

“Because Nigeria is a secular state, there is no need for it to be altogether Muslim or altogether Christian. Don’t favor a religion against another. Be neutral. Nigeria must recover equitably. Everybody should have what belongs to him, no matter the religion he practices.”

On insecurity, Bishop Oke condemned violence perpetrated in the name of religion and called for decisive government action.

“There are radicals who are bent on turning Nigeria into a caliphate state. But the constitution guarantees freedom of religion and freedom of worship,” he said.

“To use violence and kinetic means to unlawfully take lives in the name of religion — that is satanic, that is wrong. And the government should come hard on that.

“Kidnapping is criminal. Taking children from school is criminal. Beheading is criminal. If anybody is doing that in the name of religion, he is a criminal, whether he is from the Christian side or from the Islamic side.

“It is not the generality of Islam. It is the radicals among them. The Muslim community should identify those radicals and hand them over to law enforcement agencies.”

He added: “If you can persuade me to change from being a bishop into becoming a Muslim, and you succeed, God bless you. If I persuade you to convert to Christianity, God bless me. Let it be by persuasion. But if it is by violence, no. There is a difference between criminality and religion. The government must not tolerate criminality.”

The cleric also urged Nigerians to seek divine intervention for the country’s myriad challenges, including insecurity and economic hardship.

On his recent remarks regarding church titles, Bishop Oke clarified that while titles like “Senior Pastor” or “Archbishop” are not explicitly mentioned in the Bible, they are administrative necessities for organizational structure.

“The bishop is in the Bible. The evangelist is in the Bible. The archbishop is a senior bishop, or father of bishops. As the church grows and expands, structure is adjusted,” he explained.

“For administrative convenience in a growing organization, the fathers of the organization sit together and say, ‘God is not the author of confusion. All of us cannot be equal. There must be a leader. Let’s have the senior pastor.’

“That doesn’t mean it’s unbiblical. It is part of the wisdom that God gave them to cope with the growth rate that they were faced with.

“There is a difference between what is not mentioned in the Bible and what is unbiblical. It is not a sin. It evolves with growth and enlargement.”

World.title: Osun election: APC’s Oyebamiji downplays ‘federal might’, vows to banish poverty
World.content:
Oyebamiji

The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun State, Bola Oyebamiji, has dismissed allegations that the Federal Government plans to deploy its influence to secure victory for him in the August 15 governorship election.

Oyebamiji spoke during the Arise Television townhall for governorship candidates ahead of Saturday’s election, where he also outlined his plans to tackle poverty, improve security and invest in key sectors of the state.

The APC candidate said his priority, if elected, would be the welfare and development of residents across the state, irrespective of their location.

“Governance is about people, it’s not about segments. It’s not about an area. It’s not about a city. It is not about a town. It’s the entirety of the state,” he said.

Oyebamiji said his administration would prioritise security and the welfare of residents, while also seeking to address hunger and poverty through investments in agriculture, education and healthcare.

“We want to banish hunger and poverty. I want to invest seriously on agriculture, education, and health,” he said.

He added that his administration would also focus on human capital development and improve the welfare of residents.

“Human asset is very important to us; we are going to invest in human asset, we are going to look at their welfare. We are going to increase our welfare. Capital development is very important. These are the things that I’m bringing on board,” Oyebamiji said.

Reacting to Governor Ademola Adeleke’s allegation that the Federal Government was planning to deploy “federal might” to influence the election, Oyebamiji said he had not encountered evidence supporting the claim during his campaign across the state.

“I actually listened to the Mr. Governor and I can see that most of the answers to that question was not true. I have visited 30 local government areas in Osun State three times. Nobody has ever heard that,” he said.

Oyebamiji said his consultations with party members, community leaders, artisans, lawyers, traders and civil servants had convinced him that residents were seeking a change of government.

He said he also inaugurated canvassers across the state as part of efforts to mobilise support for his candidacy.

“I was convinced beyond reasonable doubt that our people in Osun are ready for a change. I’m coming here as the incoming governor of Osun, come 15th of August, 2026,” he said.

Oyebamiji maintained that his expected victory would be determined by voters rather than political influence.

“It is not by any power, whether it is a national power or it’s mighty power, it is by the people,” he said.

The APC candidate also claimed that his candidacy had received endorsements from about 42 groups across the state, including private enterprises and civil servants.

World.title: ‘Women like money, give them; they’ll like you’ – Bishop Thomas Aremu tells husbands
World.content:
Bishop Thomas Aremu

By Adewale Adesewa

Bishop Thomas Aremu, a former senior pastor and vice president of Living Faith Church Worldwide, popularly known as Winners’ Chapel, has advised men to take care of their wives financially, urging them to provide money for their spouses and attend to their needs.

Aremu gave the advice while speaking at MLF Day 1, in a video circulating online.

He said women should not be denied financial support by their husbands, particularly when they are responsible for caring for the home and children.

“Women like money, so if you have money, spend it on them. Give her money. She is the one taking care of the children, and she will like you,” he said.

Aremu also shared how he responds when his wife asks him for money, saying he may initially ask what she needs it for but would give her the money if she insists.

“Number one, she needs to have some rest. Number two, she is my wife; she is not somebody else’s wife, and I have the money,” he said.

The bishop further urged men to take care of their wives and not automatically regard their desire to buy items such as gold as ungodly.

He said: “She may see gold and say she wants to buy it. Don’t say carnality. No. The street of heaven is made up of gold, so it doesn’t destroy godliness.”

World.title: NUT raises alarm over encroachment on Teachers’ FCT land
World.content:
Pleads with Wike to intervene recover land

By Folarin Kehinde

The Nigeria Union of Teachers, NUT, Municipal Branch, Federal Capital Territory, FCT, has appealed to the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, to recover lands acquired for teachers’ estates in Abuja and investigate those allegedly behind the encroachment on the properties.

The union made the appeal at a press briefing in Abuja, alleging that land grabbers, developers and a Chinese quarry company had encroached on portions of its properties at Lugbe East Extension and Lugbe 1 Extension layouts.

The NUT said the affected plots of land were acquired and regularised in 2012 for the development of teachers’ estates but alleged that the properties had been subjected to persistent encroachment in recent years.

The Secretary of the NUT Municipal Branch, FCT, Comrade Percy Ndam, said the union had repeatedly drawn the attention of the FCT Administration and other government agencies to the encroachment of its property without receiving any positive response.

Ndam said the union had also reported the matter to the FCT Minister, the National Assembly, the Senate Committee on FCT, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission and the Federal Ministry of Education.

He said, “We want the minister to build houses for us. We want him to recover these lands. We also want him to go straight after those who are doing this grabbing.”

According to him, a committee constituted by a previous FCT administration to investigate the matter had yet to submit its report to the union.

He said, “Severally, we met with the committee. Each time we meet, they will tell us they are working on it and that government came and left.”

The NUT accused a Chinese-owned quarry company and some unidentified developers of encroaching into the portions of the land and fencing off part of the land for their own selfish use.

The union also alleged that some developers had obtained documents relating to portions of the properties after the NUT had acquired its land.

Ndam said the union had taken legal action over the alleged encroachment involving the quarry company but lamented that the matter had remained in court amid repeated adjournments.

He, however, said the union would continue to pursue peaceful and lawful means to protect the properties.

“We are teachers. We are mothers. We are responsible personalities. We cannot carry weapons to fight,” he said.

The union called for an immediate halt to alleged unauthorised activities on the two sites and the prosecution of those behind the encroachment while the FCT should revalidate and protect the land it allocated to the union.

The union said the properties represented a major welfare investment for serving and retired teachers, adding that many members had contributed from their salaries towards the acquisition and development of the land.

“This is not just land; this is the future of teachers in the FCT,” the union said.

Earlier, the Chairman of the NUT Municipal Branch, Comrade Umar Mohammed Makusidi, who was represented by the Deputy Chairman, Comrade Charles Ekwere, appealed to the public and FCT authorities to intervene in the union’s land dispute, alleging that the minister had yet to grant them an audience.

World.title: Police nab 27 year old man for allegedly defiling teenage domestic worker in Ondo
World.content:
File image.

By Dayo Johnson Akure

Police detectives in Ondo State have arrested a 27-year-old man, Solomon Onaola, for the alleged defilement of a 15-year-old domestic help.

Vanguard gathered in Akure, the state capital, that the incident occurred in Omifon, Odigbo council area of the state.

It was learnt that the guardian of the victim reported at the police station that the 15-year-old girl, who was working as a domestic help in her household, had on several occasions left home without permission.

The case was initially reported at Odigbo Divisional Police Station and was subsequently transferred to the Gender-Based Offences Unit of the Command for discreet investigation, owing to the sensitive nature of the allegation.

A police source said that when the girl was questioned about where she usually went whenever she left home, she allegedly disclosed that the suspect, Solomon Onaola, had been taking her to his late mother’s residence in Omifon, where he allegedly engaged in unlawful sexual intercourse with her.

Contacted, the state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said: “Following the report, police operatives commenced investigation and subsequently arrested the suspect.”

Abayomi added that “the victim has also been placed under appropriate care and necessary steps are being taken in accordance with established procedures for cases involving alleged sexual offences against minors.”

According to him, “the Commissioner of Police, Ondo State Command, CP Felix Ohagwu, has directed the Gender-Based Offences Unit to conduct a thorough and professional investigation into the matter, with a view to establishing the facts and ensuring that justice is served.”

He reiterated the command’s commitment to “protecting children and other vulnerable members of society from sexual exploitation, abuse and other forms of violence.”

“Parents, guardians and members of the public are equally urged to remain vigilant, pay close attention to the welfare of children under their care and promptly report any suspected case of abuse to the police,” he said.

Abayomi stated that “the suspect remains in police custody while investigation is ongoing and will be charged to court upon conclusion of investigations.”

*** Suspected armed robber arrested in Owo with firearm

Meanwhile, a 32-year-old suspected armed robber, Ogunmola Oluwasola, has been arrested with a firearm and ammunition in Owo.

The suspect was arrested by operatives of the Command’s Anti-Kidnapping Squad during a stop-and-search operation along the Owo–Ute road.

During the search, the operatives recovered one cut-to-size pistol and four rounds of live ammunition from his possession.

The suspect was immediately taken into custody, while the recovered firearm and ammunition have been secured as exhibits.

DSP Abayomi said the suspect’s statement had been obtained as detectives intensified efforts to establish the source of the weapon, his intended use of the firearm, and whether he is connected to any robbery, kidnapping or other criminal activities within Owo and its environs.

He reiterated that the Command would continue to sustain intelligence-led patrols, stop-and-search operations and other proactive security measures across the state, particularly along major highways and identified crime-prone locations.

He warned criminals and individuals who unlawfully possess or traffic in firearms that the police and other security agencies would continue to pursue them relentlessly.

“The suspect remains in police custody as investigation continues, with a view to determining his possible links to other criminal activities and bringing all persons found culpable to justice,” he said.

He assured members of the public that “the Command remains committed to protecting lives and property and will continue to deploy intelligence, visibility patrols and community-based policing strategies towards maintaining peace and security across the state.”

World.title: Osun election: I’ll give governance back to people — AAC candidate
World.content:
The governorship candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) in the Osun State governorship election, Olajide Esan, has pledged to return governance to the people if elected on August 15.

Esan made the promise during the Arise Television town hall for governorship candidates ahead of Saturday’s election, where he outlined his plans for improving accountability and citizen participation in governance.

The AAC candidate said Osun had suffered from a lack of genuine leadership despite having many politicians, arguing that leadership should be centred on service rather than the exploitation of the people’s challenges.

“Osun state deficient of leadership. Even though we have too many politicians, but we don’t have leaders because leadership is all about service,” Esan said.

He accused politicians of exploiting poverty and other challenges confronting the people, saying his administration would seek to reverse that pattern by giving residents a greater role in governance.

“If I would be going into my vision, what is important to me is to give governance back to the people, because instead of leaders to be serving the people in Nigeria, especially in Osun State, it is the people who are serving the leaders,” he said.

Esan said his administration would establish an Osun Resident Database to provide government with accurate information about residents and help in planning and delivering services.

“Part of the plans we have, we have what I call Osun resident database. This database will give us the opportunity to have the information of Osun residents and to also be able to put the right things in place for Osun people,” he said.

He also proposed a financial dashboard that would allow residents to monitor government spending and demand explanations where public funds were not properly accounted for.

“Financial dashboard will give Osun people the opportunity to monitor and to track government spendings, so that if one error happens, they can call me that youth governor. Where is our one naira?” Esan said.

According to him, greater transparency and accountability would discourage politicians from treating governance as a business venture.

“Accountability is very important. Because the lack of accountability is what is making politics a lucrative business to career politicians,” he said.

Esan added that the proposed measures would ensure that government became more responsive to residents and make it difficult for those seeking public office for personal gain to continue operating as usual.

“Once these things are there, it will no longer be business as usual for those who actually want to serve the people,” he said.

World.title: Birth Registration: 3.5m children ‘invisible’ in South-West, Edo records — Report
World.content:
Every Nigerian child must be registered — UNICEF

By Chioma Obinna & Rotimi Ojomoyela

No fewer than 3.5 million children under one year across the six South-West states and Edo State have no birth registration, leaving them without legal identity and effectively “invisible” in government records, the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, has warned.

UNICEF said the huge gap in birth registration could have serious consequences for the affected children, including difficulties accessing education, healthcare and social protection, as well as proving their age and nationality later in life.

Chief, UNICEF Lagos Field Office, Celine Lafoucriere, who disclosed this at a two-day media dialogue on birth registration of children under one year, organised by the Lagos State Office of the National Population Commission, NPC, in collaboration with UNICEF, said every child had a fundamental right to legal identity.

“Every single child in Nigeria should be registered. This is the foundational first right of a child. Every single Nigerian child needs to be registered in Nigeria,” she said.

Lafoucriere said the estimated 3.5 million unregistered children across the region represented more than a statistics gap, warning that children not captured in the civil register could also be left out when government plans and funds social programmes.

She said: “If 3.5 million children are still not registered, they will go unnoticed and there will be no government funding to support them simply because they are invisible.”

The UNICEF official explained that birth registration was not merely about obtaining a certificate but about formally establishing a child’s existence before the law.

According to her, an unregistered child could encounter difficulties accessing basic services and exercising rights throughout life.

“They do not exist for access to basic social services like education, like health. But they will also continue not to exist as they reach adult age when it is time for them to vote, to participate in political life, but also when they will be in a position to inherit their parents’ wealth.

“As they are not registered, they are invisible,” she said.

Lafoucriere identified inadequate awareness, geographical isolation, limited access to registration points and gaps in the digital registration system among factors responsible for the persistent registration deficit.

She said many parents were unaware that birth registration was free or that registration could be completed at health facilities and community-level registration points.

“Some parents are very willing to do so but it remains difficult in some geographical contexts,” she said.

According to her, UNICEF is supporting government efforts to digitalise birth registration and take the service closer to families, particularly those in underserved communities.

She urged the media to intensify public enlightenment and tell the stories of children and families affected by the registration gap.

The UNICEF official also stressed that accurate civil registration was essential to the development of an effective social protection system.

She explained that government could only adequately plan and allocate resources when it knew how many children required services.

“If we are working, and the government is working on building a social protection system, having a civil register is very important. But in that civil register, no child that is not registered at birth will exist,” she said.

Lafoucriere, however, noted that progress had been made, particularly with efforts to link birth registration to the National Identification Number, NIN, saying the development would strengthen children’s legal identity from birth.

In his welcome address, Lagos State Director of the National Population Commission, Abiola Kekere-Ekun, urged the media to move beyond reporting statistics and government activities and take the birth registration message directly to parents and caregivers.

He said reliable birth registration data was crucial for effective governance because it enabled government to determine the number and distribution of children and plan adequately for education, healthcare, social protection and other services.

Also speaking, UNICEF Child Protection Specialist, Denis Onoise, said about 24.8 million children under five had been registered across Nigeria.

He described birth registration as a critical component of children’s rights because it provides legal recognition of a child’s existence.

Onoise warned that children without birth certificates or recognised documentation could face serious difficulties proving their identity or age and accessing certain services later in life.

He called for stronger public awareness and improved access to registration services, urging parents and caregivers to register children as early as possible.

UNICEF Communication Officer, Blessing Ejiofor, said the media dialogue was aimed at strengthening journalists’ capacity to report effectively on birth registration and support advocacy for increased registration within the first year of life.

She said universal birth registration would require sustained media advocacy, stronger coordination among relevant institutions, improved accessibility of registration services and accountability by authorities.

The two-day dialogue brought together journalists from Lagos, Ogun, Osun, Ondo, Ekiti and Edo states, as well as representatives of government agencies, UNICEF, health workers and other stakeholders.

World.title: The Man Between Market and the State
World.content:
Kehinde Sowole writes on how Temi Popoola and NGX Group are turning economic reform into capital formation

Every era of economic reform produces two kinds of figures. There are the reformers themselves, the presidents, ministers and governors who take the political risk of change. And there are the interlocutors: the institutional leaders who translate reform into confidence, policy into capital, and government ambition into market reality. Nigeria’s current reform era has no shortage of the first kind. What has become increasingly evident is the emergence of the second, and few embody that role more convincingly today like Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Nigerian Exchange Group.

Last week’s engagement between the NGX Group Board and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the State House was, on its surface, a courtesy visit. Read properly, it was something rarer: a working session between a government pursuing economic transformation and a capital market leadership that has positioned the market as an increasingly indispensable instrument for delivering that transformation. The numbers presented to the president told one story; market capitalisation rising from under N30 trillion in 2023 to about N160 trillion today, while the All-Share Index climbed from roughly 52,000 to over 244,000 points. The rally reflects the positive response of investors to recent macroeconomic reforms, while also building on decades of institutional development by market operators, listed companies, regulators and investors. But the more consequential story came afterwards was the president’s affirmation that NNPC Limited will be reformed and listed on the capital market, alongside his endorsement of the market’s role in financing Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy.

That a sitting Nigerian president now speaks of the stock exchange as an instrument of national economic strategy, in the same breath as fiscal and monetary policy did not happen by accident. It reflects years of deliberate work by institutions across Nigeria’s capital market ecosystem to reposition the market from a spectator of economic policy to an active participant in national development. Throughout that evolution, Popoola has emerged as one of its most influential advocates and architects, helping to articulate a vision of the capital market not merely as a trading venue, but as infrastructure for national growth.

Consider the record. When the banking sector recapitalisation programme was announced, sceptics predicted overwhelming dependence on foreign capital. Instead, roughly three-quarters of the funds were mobilised domestically, supported by NGX Invest, a market infrastructure that NGX Group and the wider ecosystem had modernised for exactly such moments. When Nigeria migrated to T+1 settlement this June, placing it among the more efficient emerging markets in post-trade settlement, it reflected years of coordinated technical work involving exchanges, regulators, clearing institutions and market participants. When international index providers questioned aspects of the market’s structure, NGX Group’s leadership responded with evidence rather than rhetoric. And when Dangote Petroleum Refinery signalled its intention to list, it reinforced a proposition Popoola has consistently advanced: Nigeria’s largest enterprises should increasingly seek long-term capital from Nigerian markets, allowing more Nigerians to participate in the country’s economic growth.

What distinguishes Popoola’s leadership is its refusal of the adversarial posture that has often characterised relations between African markets and African governments. Exchange leaders have traditionally oscillated between supplication and criticism, either asking governments for concessions or lamenting policy shortcomings. Popoola has helped shape a different approach: partnership not with any particular administration, but with credible economic reform itself. The four priorities presented at the State House; the privatisation and listing of viable government assets, dual listings by leading Nigerian companies, clarity around capital gains tax treatment, and greater use of capital markets to finance infrastructure, were less a list of requests than a proposed division of labour. Government provides policy clarity, assets and reform momentum; the capital market provides capital formation, price discovery, transparency and broad-based ownership.

The NNPC commitment is the first major test of that division of labour, and it is difficult to overstate what it could represent. A listed NNPC would mean audited accounts where opacity has often prevailed, market discipline where political discretion has historically dominated, and perhaps most significantly, an opportunity for millions of Nigerians, directly and through their pension funds to own a stake in one of the country’s most strategic commercial enterprises. It is privatisation not as transfer to a connected few, but as broader public participation. If executed successfully, it could become one of the defining institutional reforms of this era. NGX would provide the platform, while years of investment in settlement systems, market infrastructure, retail participation and institutional capacity would help explain why the market is increasingly prepared for transactions of such scale.

None of this eliminates the difficult questions. Nigeria’s cost-of-living pressures remain real, and rising equity indices do not immediately reduce household expenses, a reality acknowledged by both Popoola and Central Bank Governor Yemi Cardoso. The trillion-dollar economy remains an aspiration requiring sustained growth well beyond recent performance. And the distance between a presidential commitment and a completed listing is one on which many reform programmes have faltered. Yet this is precisely why institutional leadership matters. Commitments become transactions only when there are credible institutions capable of executing them and leaders trusted by policymakers, domestic investors and international capital alike. That institutional credibility built patiently over time may prove to be one of the most valuable assets the Nigerian capital market possesses.

The history of successful reforming economies demonstrates that governments alone do not build vibrant capital markets, nor do capital markets reform governments in isolation. Progress emerges through productive collaboration between credible public policy and strong market institutions. That collaboration must outlast any administration because markets ultimately create wealth through rules, not rulers. The strongest testament to NGX Group’s growing institutional maturity is that its case for deeper capital markets would remain the same regardless of who occupies political office. In Nigeria’s reform moment, Popoola has become one of the principal figures helping to occupy that critical space between policy and capital. The president has now said publicly what many market participants have long believed: if the stock market is doing well, Nigeria’s economy is moving in the right direction. The task now is to ensure that confidence continues to translate into investment, reform into opportunity, and market performance into lasting national prosperity.

· Sowole, a financial expert, is based in Lagos

World.title: UBEC Urges States to Fully Utilise Basic Education Funds
World.content:
* Delta reports 90% implementation of 2025 action plan

Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) has called on states to ensure full utilisation of available funds and prompt implementation of approved programmes to improve basic education delivery across Nigeria.

The call was made during a courtesy visit to the Delta State Government, represented by Deputy Governor, Monday Onyeme, in Asaba, as part of the 30th quarterly meeting of UBEC management with executive chairmen of State Universal Basic Education Boards (SUBEBs).

The meeting, themed, ‘Repositioning Basic Education in Nigeria to Optimise Investment and Impact,’ focused on how investments and innovations can translate into better classrooms and learning outcomes.

UBEC commended Delta State for accessing its UBE matching grants up to 2025.

The commission also urged the state to take advantage of the education component of the World Bank-supported HOPE Education Programme, with up to $500 million earmarked for education.

States were told that to qualify, they must access the 2026 matching grant and implement at least 50 per cent of their 2025 Action Plan.

Responding, Onyeme said updated records showed that Delta had about N1 billion in unutilised funds, contrary to the N8 billion earlier reported.

He added that the state had implemented about 90 per cent of its 2025 Action Plan and had already received its 2026 matching grant.

The UBEC team also highlighted Delta’s technology-driven teacher attendance system, Attend360, as a model that could strengthen accountability in basic education nationwide.

“There is no education or quality learning without a good teacher or without a teacher in the classroom,” the executive secretary noted.

During a visit to the Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, UBEC called for stronger collaboration with traditional institutions.

Azinge described basic education as the foundation of Nigeria’s future and urged UBEC and SUBEBs to ensure no child, including those with disabilities and from disadvantaged backgrounds, is left behind.

UBEC assured the Asagba that it will continue working with states to ensure that investments in basic education yield visible impact in classrooms.

World.title: Industrial Action: Sheathe Your Sword, Exercise Restraint, NCAA Tells Unions
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) has pleaded with aviation unions to sheathe their sword and exercise restraint in the ongoing industrial action which has impacted passengers and other stakeholders.

The authority noted that the matter would have been addressed at the meeting convened by the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development Festus Keyamo last week, but the meeting could not hold as the airline operators failed to honour the invitation.

NCAA, in a statement on Tuesday by its Director General, Capt. Chris Najomo, stated that the appeal became necessary and will be resolved pending the return of the minister, Keyamo, who has been actively working towards resolving the issues.

Najomo assured the travelling public that flight safety remained uncompromised, adding that the authority would continue to exercise its statutory safety oversight responsibilities.

“We appeal to all parties to embrace dialogue and cooperation. We are confident that the matter will be resolved shortly and normal flight operations will resume as soon as practicable.

“The NCAA regrets the inconvenience caused to passengers and appreciates their patience and understanding,” he said.

World.title: Delta Suspends Works Commissioner over Alleged Assault on Gov’s Aide
World.content:
T6Sylvester Idowu in Warri, Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The Delta State Government yesterday suspended the state Commissioner for Works (Highway and Urban Roads), Hon. Izeze Rume Yakubu Reuben, with immediate effect.

The suspension, according to a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Dr. Kingsley Emu, is to allow security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation into allegations linking the commissioner to the recent assault of the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Protocol, Mr. Simon Mudi, popularly known as ‘Temple’.

The incident reportedly occurred at the Petroleum Training Institute (PTI), Effurun, in Uvwie Local Government Area of the state during the Delta Central meeting of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The SSG said the suspension was necessary to ensure that the investigation was conducted without interference and to establish the facts surrounding the incident.

The state government, he said, remained committed to maintaining public safety, law and order, and the sanctity of human lives under all circumstances.

Dr. Emu stressed that the government’s commitment to these principles remained unwavering, even when individuals or institutions of the state were involved.

“The suspension is expected to remain in force pending the outcome of the investigation by the relevant security agencies,” he said.

World.title: NHRC Demands Immediate Arrest, Prosecution of Sheikh Jingir Over Hate Speech
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has called for the immediate arrest and prosecution of prominent Islamic cleric, Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir, over what it described as hateful and inciting remarks capable of aggravating religious tensions ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Executive Secretary of the commission, Chief Tony Ojukwu, made the demand after the NHRC reviewed a viral video in which the cleric allegedly canvassed religiously exclusive politics and urged his supporters to obtain their permanent voter cards (PVCs) to “show their limit”.

Ojukwu, who condemned the remarks in strong terms, said the cleric’s reference to people of other faiths as “infidels”, coupled with his political exhortations, constituted a dangerous attempt to mobilise citizens along religious lines.

According to him, the statements amounted to hate speech and incitement to religious hatred, with the potential to trigger violence at a time Nigeria is preparing for another politically sensitive electoral cycle.

The NHRC boss said the remarks were inconsistent with the constitutional principles of equality, non-discrimination and peaceful coexistence, as well as Nigeria’s obligations under international human rights instruments.

“The commission finds these remarks to be hate speech and incitement to religious hatred and potential violence. At a time when we are preparing for another general election, such utterances are reckless and dangerous,” he said.

Ojukwu warned that failure by the authorities to respond decisively could encourage other influential religious and political actors to make increasingly provocative statements as the 2027 elections draw closer.

“We cannot afford to look away. If we fail to speak and act now, we embolden both Christian and Muslim clerics and other influential persons to make worse statements in the coming months. That path leads only to crisis,” he said.

Consequently, the commission called on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant authorities to immediately arrest and prosecute Jingir for alleged hate speech and incitement.

The NHRC insisted that any prosecution should be pursued irrespective of the cleric’s status or political affiliation, arguing that equal application of the law was necessary to deter others from exploiting religious sentiments for political purposes.

The commission’s intervention comes as political actors, religious leaders and civil society groups increasingly turn their attention to the potential impact of identity-based mobilisation on the 2027 electoral process.

Ojukwu further urged religious leaders, traditional rulers and politicians to abandon divisive rhetoric and instead encourage Nigerians to assess political leaders on the basis of competence, service delivery, integrity and respect for fundamental human rights.

He also called on Nigerians to reject identity politics and resist attempts to turn religious affiliation into a tool for political mobilisation.

“The commission will continue to monitor compliance and will engage with security agencies, INEC, and civil society to ensure that the 2027 elections are free from hate and violence,” he said.

The NHRC’s position adds a fresh dimension to the growing debate over the role of religious rhetoric in Nigeria’s electoral politics, particularly as political parties and prospective candidates begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

Jingir has previously been involved in controversies surrounding politically charged religious messaging.

In the run-up to the 2019 general election, he attracted criticism over a video message to followers concerning voting and religious identity.

The latest NHRC intervention therefore places renewed focus on the responsibility of influential religious figures to ensure that political mobilisation does not cross the line into rhetoric capable of threatening peaceful coexistence or electoral stability.

World.title: Journalists Urged to Harness AI to Transform Reporting
World.content:
The future of journalism is being reshaped by Artificial Intelligence (AI), offering unprecedented opportunities to enhance reporting, streamline workflows, and deliver more engaging content to readers worldwide.

The Chief Executive of Chesca Global Solutions Limited, Ms. Franca Ibuzo, stated this in a press statement, noting that “in automated news gathering, AI can scan vast amounts of data, social media feeds, and public records in real time, and help journalists identify breaking stories faster.”

According to her, during fact‑ checking and verification, with misinformation on the rise, AI tools assist in verifying sources, cross‑checking facts, and ensuring accuracy before publication.

She noted that “content personalisation and AI algorithms now tailor news delivery to readers’ interests, improving engagement and ensuring diverse perspectives reach the right audiences.”

Ibuzo added: “Multimedia enhancement, from generating graphics to transcribing interviews, AI reduces repetitive tasks, allowing journalists to focus on news writing.”

“Transcribing and translation are powered by AI, which enables newsrooms to break language barriers, making stories accessible to international audiences instantly.”

She, however, exphasised that “AI is not replacing journalists but rather it is empowering them.

“By leveraging AI responsibly, we can uphold the integrity of journalism while embracing innovation that makes reporting more efficient and impactful.”

“As media organisations adopt AI, ethical considerations remain paramount. Transparency, accountability, and human oversight are essential to ensure that technology strengthens trust rather than undermines it,” she said.

She urged “media organisations management to reiterate their commitment to advancing journalism through innovation by equipping reporters and editors with cutting‑edge tools to deliver credible, timely, and engaging news.”

World.title: NCWS Tasks Women to Vote Wisely, Seeks More Political Positions
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The National Council of Women’s Societies (NCWS) has urged women in Nigeria to mobilise and vote wisely in the 2027 general election in accordance with their conscience.

The President of NCWS, South-West Forum, Mrs. Priscilla Kuye, who made the call in her welcome address at the council’s annual conference held in Ibadan, Oyo State, said women should actively participate in the electoral process and support candidates committed to good governance, the rule of law and promotion of fundamental human rights.

According to her, the council was concerned about insecurity, kidnapping, unemployment, hunger and inadequate access to water and electricity in the country.

“We want good governance and promotion of the rule of law. We want all women and girls to be accorded their fundamental human rights in accordance with our constitution,” she said.

Kuye disclosed that the seminar, which focused on ‘Human Rights, Justice, Action for all Women and Girls in the Society’, was organised to educate women on issues affecting them, particularly ahead of the 2027 elections.

Stating that the conference brought together women from various associations across the South-west geopolitical zone.

In its communiqué, the conference called for the mobilisation and sensitisation of women to vote wisely, while advocating increased representation of women in political positions of responsibility.

The council also urged women to seek more elective and political positions while calling for the empowerment of women through access to low-interest loans to enable them to establish and expand businesses.

The NCWS further encouraged educated women to guide and support less-educated women, while calling on men to stop relegating women to the background in all spheres of life.

It also recommended increased media publicity for the council’s activities, including jingles, interviews, and other platforms to showcase the achievements of its members.

The council proposed the organisation of a mega meeting where political stakeholders and other power brokers would be invited to pledge their support for women.

The communiqué also announced plans to celebrate the centenary birthday of one of the founding mothers of NCWS and its first Secretary-General in 1962, Prof. Adetoun Ogunsheye.

Ogunsheye, according to the council, is Nigeria’s first female professor, and her centenary celebration is scheduled for December 5, 2026.

The NCWS was registered as a society on June 24, 1965, after its formation in Ibadan by women’s organisations seeking to promote women’s education, political participation and economic development.

The organisation has since expanded to all states of Nigeria with a national body.

World.title: Aviation Unions Picket Air Peace Operations, Attack Workers over Refusal to Join Associations
World.content:
*Disrupt over 70 Air Peace domestic, regional flights

*United Nigeria Airlines grounds operations in protest

Chinedu Eze

The National Union of Air Transport Employees (NUATE) and the Air Transport Service Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (ATSSSAN) early Tuesday picketed the operation of Nigeria’s leading carrier, Air Peace, at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, forcing the airline to cancel over 70 daily flights.

The unions said they are protesting against the 5% Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) owed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) but the airlines.

But NCAA had earlier confirmed that it had made agreed payment arrangement with the airlines to offset the debt which accrued when jet fuel prices spiked from N900 per litre to N3, 500 during the US-Iran war.

The unions also said the second reason why they picketed the airlines was because they refused to allow their workers join the unions.

But the unions only disrupted Air Peace operations, beat up and injured the airlines workers for refusing to join the unions. They did not give any explanation why they only targeted Air Peace operation because besides Aero Contractors and Arik Air, other domestic airlines workers are not members of any of the unions.

However, United Nigeria Airlines has suspended its operation in protest against the disruption of Air Peace flights. The airline directed its workers to suspend flight operations.

Air Peace in a statement said, “We wish to inform our esteemed passengers and the general flying public of temporary disruptions to our flight operations arising from the picketing of our airline and the ongoing industrial action by members of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (ATSSSAN), and the Trade Union Congress (TUC).

“The ongoing industrial action has resulted in the barricading of the entrances to our departure terminals at Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 1 (Alpha and Zulu Terminals) and Terminal 2 in Lagos, as well as the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport Terminal in Abuja.”

The airline further explained that the blockade has restricted access to these terminals, preventing the departure of scheduled flights from Lagos and Abuja. Consequently, passengers scheduled to travel across our network have been significantly affected by the disruption to flight operations.

“Air Peace sincerely apologises to all affected and stranded passengers for the disruption and inconvenience caused by circumstances beyond the airline’s control. Passengers scheduled to travel later today are being contacted and provided with relevant updates as the situation evolves,” the airlines said.

The Director General of NCAA, Captain Chris Najomo, said in a statement that the agency was aware of the ongoing industrial action by aviation unions and its impact on passengers and other stakeholders.

“The NCAA appeals to the unions to sheathe their swords and exercise restraint pending the return of the Honourable Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, who has been actively working towards resolving the issues. The matter would have been addressed at the meeting convened by the Honourable Minister last week, but the meeting could not hold as the airline operators failed to honour the invitation,” he said.

But the Airlines Operators of Nigeria in a statement said that they did not have issues with labour; that NCAA had directed them on what to do and both the airlines and the agency agreed on payment schedule for the debt that accumulated during the US-Iran crisis and they have been complying with the payment so, the unions have no role to play in the arrangement.

However, the unions picketing Air Peace operations beat up the airlines workers when they said they do not want to become members of the unions, but even some members of the unions admitted to THISDAY that it is not compulsory for workers to join any union.

In fact, Under Nigerian labour law, trade union membership is entirely voluntary for all workers, including those in the aviation sector. No employee can be forced to join a union or be punished for refusing to join one.

World.title: The real cost of moving to a retirement village
World.content:
When you enter your twilight years, the desire for peace and community intensifies.

A love of value for money also increases.

The retirement village satisfies the desire for community and peace, but does it deliver value?



The Cost of Living in a Retirement Village

The terms retirement village, retirement community, and retirement estate are often used interchangeably. Yet they have different costs and restrictions.

A retirement village is a community where residents, typically over 50, purchase life rights to a property.

This differs from retirement communities and lifestyle estates where residents buy a sectional title.

As part of the sectional title rules, they must meet age restrictions and other conditions for body corporate approval.

With life rights, the buyer can only occupy the property for as long as they’re alive. The developer retains control.

For a modest flat, a retiree can find a home below R500 000.



At the higher end, a house can cost R5 million in sought-after retirement villages.

Since you’re not buying a property, banks do not offer a bond.

Levies and Fees at a Retirement Village

When you join a retirement village, you agree to pay levies.

These levies typically increase by the consumer price index (CPI). But they may rise beyond this depending on the village’s needs.

As of 2026, levies range between R2 000 and R4 000.

There’s also the potential for waitlist fees.

Established retirement villages may charge these fees for individuals who want to join.

They can be one-off fees or paid annually until you secure a spot.

Retirees also pay for the amenities.

Joining a club may be free.

But residents have to pay for comforts like meals, laundry, clinic services, and transportation.

Breaking Down the Numbers

Moving to a retirement village can make sense when you consider that you don’t pay conveyancer and transfer fees. Gardening, home maintenance, security, and insurance are also free.

Being part of a community and participating in groups is also another freebie.

Yet, Life rights end when the remaining occupant passes.

It could end sooner, usually when the occupant moves out or moves to frail care.

If you choose to end the contract, you leave with nothing.

The money you’ve paid doesn’t offer you equity in the home or the estate.

Is it worth it?

To answer that question, consider how much your monthly costs will be for the duration of your stay.

The table below shows the potential cost of a life rights contract over 20 years.

Home Price Monthly Cost over 20 Years R500 000 R2 083 R750 000 R3 125 R1 million R4 167 R1.25 million R5 209 R1.5 million R6 250 R1.75 million R7 292 R2 million R8 334 R5 million R20 835

If you add your rates to this calculation, you could be paying between R4 100 on the lower end, R10 200 in the mid-range, and R26 900 on the higher end.

Then, you can contrast that with what you’ll gain if you have the title deed and what you’ll spend.

Home Monthly Costs Amount Maintenance R1 200 Insurance R1 700 Security R300 Rates R400 Community Groups R600 Total R4 200

Over 20 years, these costs total R84 000. If you include inflation, you’ll have spent R242 760 over 20 years if inflation continues on the same path.

But you will have also maintained your home and can use that capital later in life.

Could Life Rights be Worthwhile for Retirees?

As a life rights holder, your greatest benefit is the lack of fees: you don’t pay transfer or conveyancer fees.

You don’t pay to maintain or upkeep your home, nor do you pay for security. When the gardener comes to maintain your yard, you don’t pay.

Your initial payment and levies cover these costs. You can live your twilight years in peace.

But you also lose out on capital growth, an estate and control.

As a resident of a retirement village, you don’t get any voting power.

When you pass, the developer will regain control of the estate and will benefit from any capital growth.

The property cannot be inherited, and ownership cannot be transferred.

Whether this is worthwhile will depend on whether you think the upfront cost and levies justify losing homeownership in favour of amenities.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs predicted XI vs Sekhukhune United midweek
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will host Sekhukhune United at FNB Stadium on Wednesday as they look to bounce back from their disappointing MTN8 exit.

The Soweto giants suffered a 1-0 defeat to Golden Arrows in the MTN8 quarter-finals this past weekend. The result came after Chiefs had started their campaign with a 3-1 victory over newcomers Kruger United.

Fernando Da Cruz’s side must now quickly turn their attention back to the Betway Premiership, where they currently sit at the top of the table.



Chiefs will be wary of Sekhukhune, having suffered their first league defeat of last season against Ba Bina Noko after making a strong start to the campaign. They will be hoping to avoid a repeat when the two sides meet at FNB Stadium.

Another defeat could raise questions around Da Cruz and his team, while a victory would go a long way towards restoring confidence after their early MTN8 disappointment.

Kaizer Chiefs prepare for Sekhukhune battle

Chiefs could also receive a boost with the potential return of striker Flávio Silva, who missed the defeat to Arrows through injury. Mduduzi Shabalala could come into the starting XI, while Asanele Velebayi is also pushing for a start.

Luke Baartman is expected to retain his place after impressing in Chiefs’ opening two matches of the season.

In defence, Bradley Cross could return to the lineup, with Thabo Moloisane expected to continue at centre-back.

Predicted Kaizer Chiefs XI against Sekhukhune United:



Brandon Petersen; Thabo Monyane, Thabo Moloisane, Miguel Inácio, Bradley Cross; Lebohang Maboe, Adolf Mtasingwa Bitegeko; Mduduzi Shabalala; Luke Baartman, Asanele Velebayi, Flávio Silva.

Which team will claim three points?

World.title: SA bus drivers are IN DEMAND in Ireland. Nearly 100 already hired
World.content:
Drivers arriving from abroad are provided with accommodation for their first four weeks. Image: Wikimedia Commons

Dublin Bus has turned to South Africa to help tackle a shortage of drivers, with almost 100 recruits hired in recent months.

The public transport operator’s first recruitment campaign in South Africa has resulted in 93 hires, according to chief people officer Barbara Carroll.

According to the Irish Times, the new recruits are arriving in Ireland at a rate of about six a week.



The recruitment drive comes as Dublin Bus looks to fill vacancies in the Irish capital caused by staff turnover while expanding its services.

The company employs around 4 650 people, about three-quarters of whom are drivers. Its workforce includes people from roughly 90 different countries. Dublin Bus has previously recruited mechanics from Spain and the Philippines.

Language was an important factor behind the decision to recruit drivers from South Africa.



“[South Africa] is an English-speaking country and there’s a good strong pipeline of drivers,” Carroll said.

South African bus drivers tapped to fill shortage

The South African recruits already hold the licences required to drive buses. Their existing qualifications make the country particularly attractive to Dublin Bus.

“There is certain paperwork they need to do when they’re on the island of Ireland,” Carroll added.



This includes obtaining an Irish residence permit and completing the licence exchange process. Ireland and South Africa have an agreement allowing South African driving licences to be exchanged.

Dublin Bus is working with an organisation in South Africa to vet candidates before they travel to Ireland. Once there, the recruits complete the company’s training programme.

New recruits face longer training

Although the South African drivers already hold the higher category licence needed to operate buses, their training takes a bit longer than that of most new recruits.



Carroll said Dublin Bus carries out additional work to help overseas recruits integrate into the company and assimilate in Ireland.

Drivers arriving from abroad are provided with accommodation, but only for their first four weeks.

“After that, they’re on their own,” Carroll noted.



“So, it’s tough for them. They are on a training rate and they are very focused on getting through the system as quickly as they can.”

The South African recruitment campaign is unlikely to be a one-off. Dublin Bus plans to continue hiring around 200 drivers a year for the foreseeable future.

“There’s a national shortage, but we’re planning to continue the recruitment,” Carroll concluded.

World.title: NEW footage surfaces from Peet Viljoen’s shoplifting arrest (watch)
World.content:
The Florida shoplifting case involving Peet and Mel Viljoen is back in the spotlight after new footage of Peet being questioned surfaced online. Image: Screenshot

The Florida shoplifting case involving Peet and Mel Viljoen is back in the spotlight after new footage of Peet being questioned about alleged checkout irregularities surfaced online.

Journalist and content creator Bianca van Wyk shared the video on Sunday, 9 August, prompting renewed discussion around the case.

Lawd, please give me just 10% of the confidence and delusional optimism of THIS mediocre white man😂



Peet Viljoen telling a US detective that his and Mel’s arrest based on a 6 month investigation and evidence of 60 incidents is a “fishing trip”🤦🏻‍♀️ pic.twitter.com/Fiw3zjMrzK  August 9, 2026

Failed to scan

In the footage, an interviewer questions Peet about a series of transactions at a Publix supermarket in Boca Raton.

The interviewer alleges that items in the couple’s shopping carts repeatedly failed to scan correctly and claims there were more than 60 incidents that could be put to Peet.

The questioning also refers to surveillance footage that allegedly shows Peet placing a bottle of San Pellegrino underneath a case of water before it went through the self-checkout process.

Peet appears to dispute the allegations and points to possible problems with the supermarket’s self-checkout system. He argues that the system was relatively new and describes the questioning as a “fishing trip”.

When asked whether he had ever left the store without paying for goods, Peet responds: “I’ve never not paid for stuff.”

The footage provides another glimpse into the investigation that led to the couple’s arrest in Florida earlier this year.



What happened at Publix?

Peet and Mel Viljoen, known to South African audiences from The Real Housewives of Pretoria, were arrested in Boca Raton in March 2026 after investigators accused them of being involved in an alleged months-long retail theft scheme.

According to police allegations, the couple used a method known as ticket-switching, in which cheaper items were allegedly scanned instead of more expensive goods.

Investigators said the alleged activity involved dozens of transactions and more than $5 300 worth of groceries.

The allegations included claims involving products such as sparkling water and other groceries.

Sparked strong reaction online

Earlier footage from the investigation has also surfaced, including police bodycam material showing Mel being questioned by detectives about the alleged transactions.

The latest video has once again sparked a strong reaction on social media, with viewers divided over Peet’s responses during the questioning.

Comments included reactions such as:

“The confidence is honestly something else. He really does not seem shaken at all.”

“That ‘fishing trip’ line has social media talking. This case keeps getting more bizarre.”

“Whether you believe him or not, that interrogation is definitely going to spark another round of debate.”

“Every time this story seems to disappear, another video drops.”

“The internet has officially entered another episode of the Viljoen saga.”

Denied the allegations

The couple have denied the allegations and pleaded not guilty. The charges remain allegations and have not been proven in court.

With the legal proceedings continuing and more footage emerging, the case is likely to remain a subject of intense public interest in South Africa.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs handed double injury concern ahead of midweek fixture
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have two injury concerns ahead of their midweek fixture against Sekhukhune United.

Amakhosi suffered a 1-0 defeat to Golden Arrows in the MTN8 quarter-finals on Sunday, with Fernando Da Cruz’s side missing Ethan Chislett and striker Flavio Silva.

The duo featured in Chiefs’ opening 3-1 win over Kruger United, but neither was involved against Arrows.



Speaking after the defeat, Da Cruz revealed that Silva picked up an injury during training on Saturday, just a day before the match.

“First thing, [Flavio] Silva got hurt yesterday [Saturday] at training, matchday minus one,” he said.

“So, we have three games in six days, and we prefer to be careful with him – the same thing for [Ethan] Chislett also.”



Chiefs an injury concern

The Chiefs coach also explained why other attacking players, including Asanele Velebayi and Pule Mmodi, were not introduced against Arrows.

“For players like [Asanele] Velebayi and Pule Mmodi, it’s our choice [to not include them in Sunday’s game], but also we have three games in six days.

“So, we will need the whole squad for these three games because it will be a tough week for us.



“We also missed other players who are injured.

“They are in rehabilitation and periodisation, but it’s interesting for the players who are available at the moment, and they would come back step by step.”

Chiefs are also without Paseka Mako, Nkhanyiso Shinga and Khanyisa Mayo, who are currently recovering from injuries.



There is, however, positive news on Bradley Cross, who picked up an injury during pre-season and has now returned to full fitness.

Chiefs will be hoping to have Silva and Chislett available when they face Sekhukhune as they look to bounce back from their MTN8 disappointment.

Will Chiefs beat Sekhukhune?

World.title: 263 million South African browser cookies stolen by cybercriminals
World.content:
Hackers are using increasingly sophisticated methods to access online accounts. Image: canva

South Africans are being warned about a growing cyber threat that could allow criminals to access online accounts without even knowing the victim’s password.

More than 263 million browser cookies linked to South Africa have been found in infostealer datasets circulating online, according to research by cybersecurity company NordVPN.

South Africa ranked 30th globally for the number of stolen browser cookies identified in the research.



Browser cookies are small pieces of data stored on devices that allow websites to remember users, including keeping them logged in or saving shopping carts.

Cybercriminals are increasingly targeting so-called “remember-me” cookies, which can contain information linked to an authenticated session. If criminals obtain a valid session cookie, they may be able to access an account as the legitimate user, potentially bypassing password and other authentication measures.

How the ‘browser cookie’ scam works

The attack, known as session hijacking, typically starts when criminals trick users into downloading infostealer malware through phishing links, suspicious websites or social engineering.

The malware can search a device for valuable information, including browser cookies, which can then be used to hijack online sessions.

The FBI has warned that stolen cookies can allow criminals to access accounts such as Netflix, YouTube and Reddit, as well as potentially more sensitive services such as email.

More than 52 billion browser cookies stolen globally

NordVPN found more than 52 billion cookies in infostealer datasets worldwide.



The most frequently stolen records were not primarily banking-related. Google accounted for approximately 11.78 million stolen records, followed by Facebook with 8.10 million and Microsoft with 7.85 million.

Entertainment and social platforms were also heavily affected, with Twitch, Netflix, YouTube, Reddit and Bing among the frequently detected services.

By country, India recorded the most stolen cookies at 4.68 billion, followed by Brazil at 2.83 billion, the US at 2.43 billion, Indonesia at 2.1 billion and the Philippines at 1.93 billion.

South Africa’s 263 million cookies placed it 30th globally.

One particularly concerning finding was that 96% of the analysed logs came from devices that already had active security software installed.

NordVPN Chief Technology Officer Marijus Briedis said criminals are increasingly looking beyond passwords.

“It is no longer just about cracking a password. It’s about stealing the digital key that is already turned in the lock,” he said.

How to protect yourself

The FBI recommends avoiding suspicious links and regularly checking recent device login activity through the security settings of online accounts.

Users should also be cautious about downloading files or software from unfamiliar websites.

NordVPN recommends regularly clearing browser cookies, while Briedis said that if a session cookie is suspected of being stolen, logging out of affected accounts and refreshing the session can help limit the damage.

The warning is particularly important because a strong password may not protect an account if criminals have already obtained a valid session cookie.

World.title: Pensioners on chronic medication can now avoid this pharmacy problem
World.content:
Male pharmacist in surgical cap and gloves organizing shelves of medication in a pharmacy. Pexels

South African pensioners, including many SASSA beneficiaries managing chronic conditions on a fixed income, may soon spend less time in pharmacy queues thanks to specific new benefits confirmed by a major retail pharmacy chain.

Clicks has confirmed that ClubCard members automatically join the retailer’s Seniors Club once they turn 60, unlocking 4% cashback (double the standard 2%) on purchases made every Wednesday. Members also gain access to a network of over 200 Clicks Clinics nationwide, offering essential health services and screenings.

PLUS Health Assessments are covered by medical schemes, giving pensioners with scheme cover a way to monitor chronic conditions, common among SASSA Older Persons’ Grant recipients, without extra costs.



Repeat Prescriptions Simplified into Four Steps at Clicks

For pensioners on long-term medication, Clicks has detailed a repeat prescription service built around four simple steps. Many SASSA Disability Grant and Older Persons’ Grant recipients live with chronic illnesses requiring consistent monthly medication, and a streamlined system like this could cut down on repeat pharmacy visits, a frustration raised often by beneficiaries who face transport and mobility barriers.

Why This Matters For Grant Beneficiaries

These specific benefits, double cashback, 200+ clinics, and a simplified prescription process, are tied to ClubCard membership and unlock automatically at age 60.

For SASSA beneficiaries managing grants that barely stretch to cover basic needs, a 4% savings on weekly spending, combined with nearby clinic access, could offer tangible relief, even though the offer comes from a single retailer rather than a government programme.



For now, the offering remains specific to Clicks members, but it reflects a growing trend among retailers of positioning healthcare access as a loyalty benefit for South Africa’s ageing population.
