Why the task-based method matters

Older AI-exposure studies often relied on broad occupation titles, which tends to overstate risk. The México, ¿cómo vamos? approach is finer: it looks at what a person actually does hour to hour. A lawyer who drafts contracts may have high exposure to AI-assisted drafting, but a litigator who spends most of the day in court does not. This distinction is crucial for policy, because it points to retraining needs rather than blanket job losses.

The 4.9% national figure is modest compared with some international estimates, but it is not trivial. It represents roughly one in twenty Mexican workers, concentrated in specific sectors such as back-office services, accounting, and customer support. The study’s authors likely intend the number as a baseline for discussion, not a forecast. For employers, the implication is that job descriptions will need to evolve; for workers, the message is that task-level skills, not job titles, will determine vulnerability.

The BMV’s 24-hour trading question: a separate, quieter debate

Separately, the Mexican Stock Exchange has signalled movement toward 24-hour trading, a structural change that would align it with international venues such as London and other major venues. The available research does not confirm a specific timeline or the full rationale, so details remain uncertain. What is clear is that the BMV is exploring extended hours, likely to capture demand from international investors who trade Mexican assets during US or Asian sessions.

If implemented, 24-hour trading would affect liquidity, volatility, and operational risk. It would require changes in clearing, settlement, and market-making arrangements. For a market that has traditionally operated on a standard business-day schedule, this is a significant operational undertaking. The move would also respond to a broader push for global trading continuity, though whether it succeeds depends on regulatory approval and on whether enough participants want to trade Mexican equities at 3 a.m. local time.

What to watch next for AI exposure in Mexico

The AI-exposure study and the BMV plan are not directly connected, but they share a common thread: Mexico is adapting to a faster, more automated environment. On the labour side, the next step will be tracking whether the 4.9% figure changes as AI capabilities improve. The observatory’s methodology is designed to be updated, so future editions could show which occupations move in or out of the high-exposure category.

For the BMV, the key questions are about timing and execution. Without confirmed details, observers should treat the 24-hour plan as exploratory. What matters is that the exchange is at least considering the shift, which itself signals that Mexican financial infrastructure is preparing for a more globalised, always-on trading environment. Neither development is a headline-grabbing transformation, but both merit close attention from anyone with a stake in Mexico’s economic trajectory.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the 4.9% figure mean those jobs will disappear? No. The México, ¿cómo vamos? analysis explicitly states that medium or high exposure to generative AI does not mean the job will disappear. It means a significant share of the tasks in that occupation could be performed or facilitated by AI with current capabilities. Why are more women affected than men? The study estimates 7.7% of female workers are in exposed roles versus 3% of male workers. This likely reflects occupational segregation: women are overrepresented in clerical, administrative, and certain professional jobs that involve more routine, language-based tasks which generative AI can currently handle. When will the BMV start 24-hour trading? The timeline is not confirmed in the available research. The exchange has signalled movement toward the plan, but specific dates, regulatory steps, and the full rationale have not been verified. Treat the initiative as exploratory until official announcements are made.

Sources: México, ¿cómo vamos?; Forbes México; Infobae; Aristegui Noticias.

World.title: Costa Rica President Declares Security and Intelligence Information a ‘State Secret’
World.content:
President Laura Fernández has placed a broad range of Costa Rican security and intelligence information under a “State Secret” designation, restricting public access to records involving some of the most powerful security bodies and extending the secrecy to budgets, contracts and government procurement. The Executive Decree was signed by Fernández and Public Security Minister Gerald Campos on July 27 and took effect when it was published in La Gaceta.

The decree covers reports, documents, files and other information connected to the National Public Security Council, the National Intelligence and Security Directorate, known as the DIS, and the government group called Fuerza Élite, or Elite Force. It also reaches other security and national defense operations coordinated directly by the Presidency.

The scope goes well beyond active police investigations. Meetings, recordings, plans, logs and agreements can now be classified, along with information about police tactics, intelligence methods, operational capabilities, command structures, technology, intervention protocols, emergency response plans and systems used to evaluate the reliability of security personnel.

Perhaps most significantly for government transparency, the decree also covers spending and procurement. Entire administrative files related to security purchases can be restricted, including preliminary studies, technical requirements, bids, contract awards, financing arrangements, contracts and the execution of those contracts. The rule applies whether the government is dealing with another public institution, a private company, a consortium or a foreign contractor.

Fuerza Élite is one of the most directly affected groups. It brings Fernández together each Monday with the ministers of Public Security and Justice and Peace, the DIS leadership, chiefs of police forces under the Executive Branch and government advisers to coordinate the response to organized crime. Discussions, documents and agreements produced through those meetings now fall under the secrecy order.

The government argues that the restrictions are necessary because Costa Rica is facing increasingly sophisticated criminal organizations involved in drug trafficking, contract killings, money laundering and other forms of organized crime. Authorities say releasing operational details could expose current or future investigations, reveal weaknesses in police operations, place officers and other people at risk and damage cooperation with foreign security agencies.

Information about intelligence techniques and internal controls could also help criminal organizations identify government vulnerabilities or learn how authorities detect corruption and criminal infiltration. The decree reaches people outside government as well. Ministers, police chiefs, advisers, support personnel and public employees who encounter classified material must keep it confidential. Private consultants and contractors working with the covered agencies must sign clauses formally subjecting them to the State Secret rules.

Those covered by the measure are prohibited from revealing, reproducing, transmitting, sharing or selling protected information. The decree says their confidentiality obligation continues indefinitely, even after they leave government employment or a government contract ends. Violations can lead to administrative or criminal consequences and, for contractors, immediate termination of their agreements with the government.

The breadth of the decree, however, raises a significant constitutional question. Article 30 of Costa Rica’s Constitution guarantees public access to government offices for information on matters of public interest, while specifically exempting State Secrets. The General Police Law also provides that internal DIS reports and documents are confidential and allows the president to declare them State Secrets.

But previous Constitutional Chamber jurisprudence has taken a restrictive view of how that exception can be used. In a 2007 ruling, the court said State Secrets are an exception to the constitutional principles of government transparency and publicity and therefore must always be interpreted narrowly.

The same decision said restrictions on the constitutional right of access to public information are generally matters reserved for legislation and criticized the Executive Branch’s historical practice of declaring information secret through individual decrees in the absence of a comprehensive State Secrets law.

That distinction could become important because Decree 45870 does considerably more than protect intelligence reports or plans for an upcoming police raid. It places broad categories of spending, contracting, meetings and administrative activity outside ordinary public scrutiny.

Costa Rica’s National Archives Law provides another limit: documents classified as State Secret or restricted access lose that status after 30 years. That is separate from the new decree’s provision saying an individual’s personal obligation not to disclose protected information continues indefinitely.

The timing is also notable, although the dates matter. The decree was signed July 27, before the August 4 disclosure of an internal Ministry of Public Security intelligence report examining 122 police officers in southern Costa Rica, with observations about possible organized-crime links involving 116 of them. The publication of the decree in La Gaceta came less than a week after that report became public, but the decree itself predates the disclosure.

The State Secret order is now in force. Whether its unusually broad reach, particularly over public spending and contracting, survives constitutional scrutiny may be the next question

World.title: Rescue Center Raises $20,000 to Stop Wildlife Electrocutions
World.content:
The Jaguar Rescue Center has finished a fundraising campaign with the organization Ma Earth that raised $20,000 to insulate 50 electrical transformers in Costa Rica’s South Caribbean, in an effort to reduce wildlife electrocutions in the region.

The money will buy insulation material that the Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad will install at the locations recording the most electrocutions, known as hot spots. The center, which operates near Puerto Viejo de Talamanca in Limón province, began the project 17 years ago after it started receiving electrocuted primates and sloths, which it describes as among the most difficult rescues it handles.

Encar García, who founded the center with biologist Sandro Alviani, said these accidents almost always end in euthanasia, amputation or months of recovery, and frequently leave orphaned young when a mother is electrocuted. In one recent week the center received seven electrocuted animals.

The scale of the problem extends well beyond the Caribbean. International Animal Rescue Costa Rica reports close to 100 electrocuted animals a year in the Nosara area alone, while the Jaguar Rescue Center took in 53 animals in 2024. Rescue centers around Costa Rica receive animals affected by electrical discharge every three to five days, and roughly 90% of electrocuted animals die.

The voltages involved explain why. A domestic shock at 110 volts is painful to a person; animals on distribution lines encounter between 2,500 and 35,000 volts, according to Francisco Sánchez, veterinary director at International Animal Rescue. The animals most often affected are howler monkeys, sloths and tamanduas, species that use power lines as improvised bridges because habitat fragmentation has left them without continuous canopy to travel through. They do not distinguish between a vine and a cable.

García said the center has imported materials from the United States to test which types of insulation perform best on transformers, working alongside the ICE to solve the specific problem of sloths reaching across contact plates with their long arms. She described the two organizations as pioneers in that testing, and said the collaboration has produced substantial improvement.

Electrocutions nevertheless continue to rise, she said, because no legislation requires new construction to use insulated or buried cable. The absence of a regulatory plan governing development in the South Caribbean compounds the problem, leaving the pace of new electrical infrastructure effectively unmanaged in one of the country’s fastest-growing tourism corridors.

A legal instrument already exists on paper. Executive Decree No. 44329, published in January 2024, requires all electrical utilities to prevent and mitigate wildlife deaths on their networks, setting out measures including insulation on cabling and transformers, metal cones to block access to lines, aerial wildlife crossings, tree pruning and the tallying of animal-related faults to identify priority zones. Conservation organizations campaigning under the banner “Esto NO es Pura Vida” have said implementation has been close to nonexistent more than a year after the decree took effect.

Separately, the Legislative Assembly approved a wildlife crossings bill in second debate by 56 votes to zero. Another bill, introduced in 2022 by former Frente Amplio legislator Ariel Robles, adds a new Article 31 bis to the Organic Environmental Law and requires all public infrastructure, new or existing, to guarantee safe passage for wildlife where technical evidence shows roads are fragmenting habitat. The measure becomes law once signed at Casa Presidencial, after which the Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación will have 24 months to begin identifying natural crossing points on roads already in operation.

There is evidence the combined approach works. Research by Inés Azofeifa and Tremaine Gregory found that after 111 aerial crossings were installed between 2015 and 2021 alongside insulated cabling at Playa Hermosa in Guanacaste, the local mantled howler monkey population rose from 59 to 99 individuals while annual deaths fell from five to one.

The Jaguar Rescue Center receives no government funding and operates on donations, community support and entrance fees, taking in around 1,000 animals a year. This is not its first campaign to pay for insulation on transformers and lines, and and on current evidence it will not be its last.

World.title: Costa Rica Runs Its National Evacuation Drill Wednesday
World.content:
At 10 a.m. Wednesday, offices, schools, hotels, clinics and government buildings across Costa Rica will empty into the street at the same time. Nothing will be wrong.It is the eighth national evacuation drill, and if you are in a building when it starts, someone will ask you to leave it. Follow them, take the stairs, and expect to be back at your desk or in your room within ten or fifteen minutes.

You do not need to have signed up to be swept along by it. If your hotel, your child’s school or your workplace registered, you are taking part whether or not anyone told you in advance.If you want to actually use the exercise rather than just stand outside for it, there are three steps.

Register at simulacro.cr, write or update an emergency plan for your household or business, then evacuate at 10 a.m. Wednesday and report that you did it through the Simulacro CR app. The middle step is the one that matters and the one most people skip. A plan means deciding now who collects the children, where everyone meets if the house is unsafe, which route you take if the usual road is blocked, and what you would grab on the way out.

Standing in a parking lot for ten minutes teaches you nothing if you have never answered those questions. This year’s exercise works differently from previous ones. Rather than everyone rehearsing the same scenario, you practice for the hazard that can actually reach where you are. Eight are on the list — earthquake, flood, landslide, volcanic eruption, tornado, hurricane, fire and tsunami.

The reason for this change is more common sense than anything else. Practicing a tsunami evacuation in Cartago is wasted effort, and practicing an earthquake drill on a beach where the real problem is the water arriving twenty minutes later teaches the wrong reflex. What you rehearse should match what is likely to happen where you live.

Unfortunately, turnout is running behind last year. The emergency commission counted 350,000 people signed up as of August 3, against more than 1.4 million who took part in 2025 — the highest participation on record. Keep in mind that registration and participation are not the same thing and sign-ups tend to surge in the final days, but the gap is wide.

Alejandro Picado, president of the Comisión Nacional de Emergencias, has pointed to emergencies elsewhere as the argument for taking it seriously, noting that Costa Rica deals with emergencies constantly and that knowing how to act is a civic responsibility rather than an optional extra.

Expect some public services to slow. The Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones will run the drill at its main offices, its warehouse in Desamparados, the Civil Registry archive in Los Yoses and all 32 regional offices, with more than a thousand people involved at the main site alone, including members of the public who happen to be mid-transaction. If you have paperwork to do Wednesday morning, do it early or do it Thursday.

The app is worth downloading before Wednesday rather than during it. It carries information about the exercise and is how you log your participation afterward, which is how the commission measures who actually took part. Monday’s magnitude 7.4 earthquake in Colombia, which killed more than a hundred people and closed three airports, is a reminder of why Costa Rica runs this exercise at all. Emergencies do not schedule themselves, and the ten minutes you spend outside on Wednesday are the cheapest preparation available.

World.title: San Pedro drug sweep uncovers 59 gram suspected crack stash under vehicle
World.content:
San Pedro drug sweep uncovers 59 gram suspected crack stash under vehicle

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The evening sweep through San Pedro’s DFC area struck twice. Half an hour after intelligence led officers to a stash hidden in a palm tree, a second search across the neighbourhood uncovered an even larger cache, 59.3 grams of suspected crack cocaine, concealed beneath an old Polaris vehicle in an empty lot, bringing the night’s combined haul to nearly 90 grams.

According to the Belize Police Department, at 7:30 p.m., acting on Special Branch intelligence, a search for illegal drugs and ammunition was conducted at an empty lot in the DFC area of San Pedro Town.

While conducting the search, an officer’s attention was drawn to an old Polaris, and further checks underneath the vehicle led to the discovery of a black plastic bag. The bag was retrieved and opened, revealing a transparent plastic bag containing a white buffy substance suspected to be crack cocaine.

No one was in the immediate area at the time of the finding, and the suspected drugs were transported to the San Pedro Police Station.

At the station, the suspected crack cocaine was weighed, amounting to 59.3 grams. It was placed in a manila envelope, properly labelled, sealed, and handed over as found property to the exhibit keeper.

The find came on the heels of the evening’s first discovery, 30.49 grams of suspected crack retrieved from between a small palm tree at an abandoned location in the same area at about 7:00 p.m., placing the sweep’s total at 89.79 grams, by far the largest combined crack seizure in the country’s recent ledger of stash clearances.

No arrests have been made in connection with either find, and the matters remain under police attention.

World.title: 30 grams of suspected crack found hiding where nobody was standing
World.content:
30 grams of suspected crack found hiding where nobody was standing

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Police intelligence has led officers to the largest suspected crack cocaine find in recent weeks, with more than 30 grams recovered from a hiding spot between a small palm tree at an abandoned location in the DFC area of San Pedro Town, and no one around to claim it.

According to the Belize Police Department, on Monday, August 10, 2026, at approximately 7:00 p.m., personnel of the GI3 unit, acting on intelligence, conducted a search for drugs and ammunition at an abandoned DFC area location.

During the search, an officer’s attention was drawn to a small clear transparent bag concealed between a small palm tree. The bag was retrieved and found to contain a white buffy substance suspected to be crack cocaine.

No person was seen in the immediate area, and the find was transported to the station for processing.

At the station, the suspected crack cocaine was weighed, amounting to 30.49 grams. It was placed inside a manila envelope, properly labelled, sealed, and handed over as found property.

No arrests have been made, and the matter remains under police attention.

World.title: Light bill argument escalates to five inch knife threat
World.content:
Light bill argument escalates to five inch knife threat

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A dispute over an extension cord and a light bill escalated into a knife threat in San Pedro Town on Monday night, and a woman is now detained pending a charge of aggravated assault after allegedly pointing a five-inch blade at an 18-year-old neighbour who came to reconnect his family’s power.

According to the Belize Police Department, the young man, an electrician of the DFC area, reported that on Monday, August 10, 2026, he arrived home from work at about 8:00 p.m. to find the lights on in the house he shares with his parents. At about 8:20 p.m., the lights went out, and his father asked him to go outside to the steps to connect the extension, as the woman living upstairs was plugging it out.

According to his report, he went to the steps toward the second floor and stood about four feet from the upstairs veranda when he heard knocking. Looking up, he saw a woman knocking the wall with a silver-looking blade knife with a black handle, measuring about five inches in length.

The woman told him that they had not yet paid for the light, so he could not connect the extension, the report states. When he replied that his parents had already paid and that he could connect it, the woman allegedly told him, “if you connect the extension you wah see,” while pointing the knife at him.

The young man went downstairs to his room and informed his parents, who called the police. Officers arrived shortly after, detained the woman, and escorted her to the San Pedro Police Station.

A statement was recorded from the complainant, and a 36-year-old woman of the DFC area is detained pending a charge of aggravated assault, with an acknowledgement form issued.

World.title: San Pedro bike thief picked the wrong shop to steal from
World.content:
San Pedro bike thief picked the wrong shop to steal from

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A San Pedro Town mother’s bicycle vanished from in front of a shop in the ten minutes her daughter spent inside, but video footage, quick police work, and a recovered cruiser have turned the theft into a formal charge, with the bicycle already identified and back in evidence.

According to the Belize Police Department, a 28-year-old shelf attendant of the Boca del Rio Area reported at the San Pedro Police Station on Monday, August 10, 2026, that on Saturday morning, at about 11:30 a.m., she sent her daughter to a mini shop in the area on her red female-frame beach cruiser bicycle, valued at $400.

The child returned about ten minutes later with the news no errand should end with: someone had stolen the bicycle from in front of the store.

The investigation moved on evidence. Video footage was obtained from the shop, from which police identified a suspect. A statement was recorded from the complainant, who requested court action, and a 22-year-old construction worker of the Mosquito Coast area was detained, cautioned, informed of the reason for his detention, and escorted to the San Pedro Police Station, where his rights in custody were explained in a language he understood and he signed the acknowledgement form of his own free will.

The trail then led to the bicycle itself. The detained man was escorted to a residence in the Boca del Rio area, where a resident handed over a red female-frame beach cruiser that had been left at his home. The bicycle was taken to the station and labelled as an exhibit, and the complainant, contacted and shown the bicycle, identified it as hers.

On Monday at 5:30 p.m., police obtained a warrant in the first instance and formally arrested and charged Kevin Hernandez, 22, a Belizean construction worker of Mosquito Coast, San Pedro Town, with the crime of theft. Cautioned after the charge, he chose to remain silent.

World.title: Belize gets soaked next: up to 4 inches of rain on the way
World.content:
Belize gets soaked next: up to 4 inches of rain on the way

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belize’s stretch of gentle weather has ended. An approaching tropical wave has prompted the National Meteorological Service to issue an Excessive Rainfall Watch, with 2 to 4 inches of rain possible over the country during the next 24 to 48 hours, especially over the south, alongside a Small Craft Caution as seas turn rough.

According to the National Meteorological Service, the tropical wave will support wet and unstable weather. Skies will be cloudy today with a few sunny breaks, remaining cloudy tonight, with outbreaks of showers and thunderstorms developing over most areas, and more so over the south and central areas.

The Excessive Rainfall Watch is the day’s most important item. Rainfall of up to 2 to 4 inches is possible, with the south facing the greatest amounts, and residents are advised to monitor the weather situation and stay tuned for any flooding updates from the National Hydrological Service or NEMO. Southern communities still recovering from July’s floods should take particular note, as saturated ground and swollen creeks need far less rain to cause trouble the second time.

At sea, a Small Craft Caution is also in effect, warning of gusty winds and locally rough seas near heavy showers and thunderstorms. Winds will blow from the east to north at 10 to 20 knots, with moderate to rough seas and waves of 4 to 7 feet. Operators of small crafts should exercise caution, and postponing non-essential trips is the wiser play.

The cloud cover eases the heat. Temperatures along the coast will reach a high of 87 degrees Fahrenheit (31 Celsius) and a low of 82 (28 Celsius). Inland areas will reach 92 degrees Fahrenheit (33 Celsius) and drop to 74 (23 Celsius). In the hills, expect a high of 81 degrees Fahrenheit (27 Celsius) and a low of 68 (20 Celsius).

Critically, the reassurance holds: tropical cyclone formation is not expected in the region over the next 48 hours. This is a rain event, not a developing storm.

Looking ahead to Wednesday and Wednesday night, outbreaks of showers and thunderstorms continue to develop over most areas during the day, then gradually decrease at night.

Today’s high tides are at 8:24 AM and 9:50 PM, with a low tide at 3:48 PM and another low at 2:50 AM tomorrow. The sun rose at 5:34 AM and will set at 6:20 PM. The forecast was issued by forecaster Catherine Cumberbatch.

World.title: Two men injured after licensed gun owner fires warning shots during San Pedro altercation
World.content:
Two men injured after licensed gun owner fires warning shots during San Pedro altercation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a shooting incident in San Pedro Town after two young men reported sustaining gunshot injuries during an altercation involving several persons early Sunday morning.

Police responded to Lion Street at approximately 1:45 a.m. on August 9, where they spoke with 29-year-old mechanic Francisco Daniel Nah.

According to police, Nah reported that he was at a store when two golf carts arrived and their male occupants became involved in a verbal altercation, during which bottles were thrown.

Nah told investigators that one of the men approached him and reached toward his waist, leading him to believe that the man was retrieving a firearm. Fearing for his life, Nah, who police say is licensed to carry a 9mm pistol, fired three warning shots into the ground.

The occupants of the golf carts subsequently left the area.

However, at approximately 1:30 p.m. later that day, 20-year-old Rennel Aguilar and 19-year-old Edwin Barco reported to police that they had sustained gunshot injuries during the incident. Both men were taken for medical treatment.

Police have not indicated whether investigators have established what caused the men’s injuries or whether they were struck by rounds fired from Nah’s licensed weapon.

The investigation continues.

World.title: Two 19-year-olds hospitalized following Dangriga shooting
World.content:
Two 19-year-olds hospitalized following Dangriga shooting

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a shooting in Dangriga Town that left two 19-year-old men hospitalized on Saturday night.

Police say that at approximately 8:30 p.m. on August 8, officers visited the Southern Regional Hospital after receiving reports of a shooting and found Kevon Higinio and Jim Mendez, both of Dangriga, suffering from apparent gunshot wounds.

Initial investigations indicate that Higinio had just left an establishment when he was approached by two male persons who opened fire in their direction, injuring both Higinio and Mendez.

Both men were listed in stable condition and remained hospitalized under observation.

Police investigations into the shooting continue. The incident and identities of the two injured men have also been reported by local media.

World.title: Post-mortem confirms Samuel Chi died from drowning; police investigation continues
World.content:
Post-mortem confirms Samuel Chi died from drowning; police investigation continues

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police say a post-mortem examination conducted on fisherman Samuel Chi has determined his cause of death to be asphyxia due to drowning, while toxicology results remain pending.

Chi disappeared at sea along with Albert Vaccaro after the men went on a fishing trip on Sunday, August 2 and failed to return as expected.

A joint search involving the Belize Coast Guard and other authorities was launched, and Vaccaro was found alive the following day floating in waters southwest of Hicks Caye. Authorities said at the time that he was dehydrated and disoriented and was unable to provide a clear account of what had occurred.

Chi remained missing until his body was recovered the following morning in waters west of Hicks Caye.

During Monday’s police press briefing, authorities said the forensic pathologist found the cause of death to be asphyxia due to drowning. Police indicated that the post-mortem did not establish evidence of violence.

However, investigators are still trying to determine the circumstances that led to Chi and Vaccaro ending up in the water.

Police could not confirm during the briefing whether investigators have since obtained a comprehensive statement from Vaccaro, noting that he was initially too disoriented to provide investigators with much information.

Chi’s family has publicly raised questions about the circumstances surrounding his death and expressed suspicions that foul play may have been involved.

Police say the investigation remains ongoing.

World.title: Tougher water fines
World.content:
Water level in the Mona reservoir last week.

SEVEN parishes will face a water prohibition from Monday, August 17 as the Government moves to tighten restrictions amid worsening drought conditions.

At the same time, Minister of Water, Environment and Climate Change Matthew Samuda is set to approach the executive and legislature to punish violators with stiffer fines.

“As we had to do after the first incident that took place with Rio Cobre, where we had to shift the fine, we now have to take the same approach with fines in relation to water prohibition,” Samuda told the Jamaica Observer on Monday.

“Because of the present forecast and warning associated with El Niño, we will have to move with unprecedented speed, and we will have to engage first the Cabinet and then Parliament in the coming weeks to facilitate this,” Samuda added.

On Monday, Samuda’s ministry, through the National Water Commission (NWC), announced that the water prohibition orders will apply to Kingston, St Andrew, St Thomas, St Mary, Portland, St Ann, and St Catherine and will remain in force until further notice.

“Under the orders, no person shall use or cause water supplied by the NWC to be used for non-essential or unusual purposes. Prohibited activities include:

• irrigation or watering of gardens, lawns, grounds, and farms;

• refilling or supplying of ponds or swimming pools and/or for use other than normal domestic services such as drinking, cooking, washing, bathing, and sanitation;

• washing of vehicles by the use of a hose;

• watering or washing of roadways, pavements, paths, garages, or out-rooms;

• any activity requiring excessive or unusual quantities of water,” the ministry release stated.

The ministry said the decision followed a high-level stakeholder meeting earlier Monday with the NWC and the Meteorological Service, which confirmed that rainfall levels remain critically low and temperatures continue to soar.

Underscoring the necessity of the measure, Samuda said, “We understand that there is some disproportionate economic impact on commercial operations, such as car washes, and we have not taken this decision lightly. Ultimately, our priority is to maintain supply to critical services, especially schools, as we prepare for the September reopening.”

He further advised that sanctions will be applied to individuals and entities found in breach of the prohibition order, noting “these penalties are intended to ensure compliance and protect the integrity of Jamaica’s water supply during this critical period”.

The current fine for breaching an NWC prohibition order is $1,000. Failure to pay the court-ordered fine results in imprisonment for up to 30 days.

Samuda’s reference to the Rio Cobre was the action taken by the Government after chemical spills that resulted in fish kills that affected several species and impacted other aquatic organisms four years ago.

In January 2025 he successfully piloted a Bill in the House of Representatives which approved amendments to the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA) Act and the Wild Life Protection Act to allow for significant increases in fines and related custodial sentences.

Under the Acts, depending on the severity of the offence, as adjudicated by the Supreme Court, corporate bodies may now be subject to a fine of approximately $10 million, individuals in breach of the Acts may face a fine of up to $5 million or serve a term of imprisonment up to five years, subject to the jurisdiction of the parish courts.

On Monday, Samuda told the Observer that the request he will be taking to Cabinet and Parliament is to “move the fines in line with what was done for bodies corporate and individuals under the NRCA Act breaches.

The naturally-occurring El Niño climate pattern, which began in June and is expected to peak later this year, has already amplified unprecedented temperatures across the world.

Some 33 countries recorded their hottest July since records began, according to a detailed analysis of billions of data points from Copernicus’s ERA5 climate model.

The severe drought has triggered food security concerns worldwide.

Last week, the United Nations World Food Programme said that Central America is expected to be the region hardest hit in terms of the relative increase in food insecurity.

Including the Caribbean, the agency estimates that an additional 16 million people could face food insecurity by the end of 2027.

World.title: Who hurt the child?
World.content:
AN announcement by the Child Protection and Family Services Agency (CPFSA) that it is fast-tracking the installation of security cameras at Glenhope Place of Safety, even as it probes the injuries suffered by a one-year-old boy who had been in its care, has been welcomed by attorney Denise Hinson who is adamant that somebody needs to be held accountable for how the child came to be injured in such a manner.

“The questions still need to be answered. This should not be pushed under the rug. I’m angry, and I think that someone needs to explain why a one-year-old defenceless child, a Jamaican child, looks as if he was in an MMA (mixed martial arts) fight,” Hinson told the Jamaica Observer on Monday.

The attorney is representing the mother of the child who is before the court for immigration issues.

She said the child’s injuries captivated the attention of the St Catherine Parish Court last Friday when the matter was called up before Justice Roneiph Lawrence.

Hinson said the child’s Haitian mother, Fabienne Cherisma, who was recently arrested for overstaying her visa alongside her husband who is said to have used fraudulent documents to obtain Jamaican citizenship, were on Friday brought before the court so it could make a further order for the child to remain in the custody of the State.

However, Hinson said when the child was presented to the court, both parents went into shock.

“The child was taken to court with [healing] black and blue bruises under both eyes; what seemed to be burn marks to the right cheek and chin; swelling of the face, especially to the right cheek; and scratches to the nose. Both eyes were bloodshot in the corners. A medical shown to the court by the CPFSA officer who brought the baby to court, described the injuries as ‘non-accidental’,” Hinson told the Observer.

The attorney said that when the mother saw her child she “screamed and began to cry uncontrollably and the father collapsed. They had to be removed and later returned to the dock”.

Hinson said the court was also “visibly disturbed by the doctor’s findings and the injuries on the baby’s face”.

She said the CPFSA officer, when pressed by the judge about the cause of the child’s injuries, “informed the court that when she asked, on arriving to collect the child, she was told that he had hit his face on the crib”.

The attorney, in making a successful bail application on behalf of the mother, who was released on humanitarian grounds, however countered that, “both eyes were bruised and that could not have occurred if the child simply fell out his crib”.

“I also pointed out that the child is in danger where he is and that he needed his mother. My focus is really to get to the bottom of how the child received those injuries at Glenhope. Also, the bruises were healing and the burn mark almost completely healed. However, the child didn’t see a doctor until the day before court, on August 6, 2026. I need help in finding out when and how the child was injured and why the child wasn’t taken to the doctor until the day before the scheduled court date,” Hinson declared.

The attorney said she is in discussion with the child’s mother to determine the legal options available to her as she presses for answers regarding her son’s health. Hinson told the Observer that her client is adamant that the “child was in perfect health when removed from [their] home”.

The CPFSA issued a statement to the media on Monday saying “the incident is being investigated and is being treated with utmost urgency and importance”.

The agency stated that it “takes a zero-tolerance approach to all forms of child abuse” and said, based on the outcome of the investigation, it stands ready to execute all measures or sanctions regarding child abuse, in keeping with the Child Care and Protection Act (CCPA 2004).

Furthermore, the CPFSA said under its 2025–2027 strategic framework it established an islandwide initiative to equip residential child care facilities with security cameras, ensuring high safety standards are maintained across all locations.

“In light of the recent incident however, deployment has been prioritised to fast-track installation at the facility in which this incident has taken place,” the agency pledged.

World.title: Rock-born DJ Damage scores BMI Trailblazers award
World.content:
DJ Damage BMI Award.

JAMAICAN-BORN Leonard “DJ Damage” Douglas is celebrating career-defining achievements as the creative force behind Without You, a chart-topping single by Jevon Dewand and The Trap Starz.

The single, which reached #1 on Billboard’s Gospel Airplay Chart in February, was recognised as one of the year’s most-performed gospel songs at the Broadcast Music, Inc (BMI) Trailblazers of Gospel Music Awards on July 21 in Nashville, Tennessee.

The milestones are an international breakthrough for DJ Damage, whose two-decade career has taken him from Jamaica’s sound system culture to the global music stage.

The Atlanta-based DJ played a multidimensional role in the success of Without You, which is recognised as an urban, hip hop praise anthem, contributing as a songwriter, scratch DJ, producer, background vocalist, and featured performer in the accompanying music video.

The Billboard #1 capped an extraordinary 33-week run that saw Without You reshape the gospel and urban radio landscape, including a 12 per cent surge in radio spins during its climb to the top spot, and a #26 placement on the Billboard Year-End Top Gospel Airplay Chart.

“Reaching the Billboard #1 spot was nothing short of a dream come true. For a kid from Jamaica to achieve that level of recognition on one of music’s most prestigious charts is a milestone I don’t take lightly,” he said. “It represents both my personal achievement and a moment of pride for Jamaica and the Caribbean as a whole. Very few creatives from our region have ever stood at that height, and I’m deeply grateful and humbled to be among them.”

DJ Damage has built a career behind the scenes of the music industry, spinning for Grammy Award-winning R&B group 112; touring with American rap rock band Gym Class Heroes; and sharing stages with artistes including Swizz Beatz, DJ Khaled, Rick Ross, Ashanti, Sean Paul, Vybz Kartel, Mavado, Buju Banton, Beenie Man, and Bounty Killer.

Jevon Dewand credits DJ Damage’s versatility and musical instincts as key ingredients in the success of

Without You.

“He has a great ear for music. Sight is a blessing and vision is a gift. I saw the vision in him,” said Dewand. “DJ Damage knows all types of music, and he’s very versatile in all genres. Most DJs play music but can’t make it music. He can.”

While Billboard recognition and the BMI Award mark two of the biggest moments of his career, DJ Damage says the journey began in Prospect, Clarendon, where he first dreamt of making it in music. His breakthrough came years later in Stony Hill, St Andrew, when he convinced promoters to let him perform with R&B group 112.

“That night in Stony Hill was everything. It was me taking a chance and betting on myself. I knew that if I could just get my foot in the door and get on that stage with 112, my skills would reach the right ears,” he said.

They did.

“I still DJ for 112 to this day. From there I took the momentum to Jersey City and began DJ’ing with Gym Class Heroes, and it just kept building. Every connection, every show, and every risk led to the next opportunity. I went on to DJ for Shai, joined a sound system called Diamond Movements, and had the privilege of performing alongside legends across reggae, dancehall, R&B, hip hop, and more. That one night in Stony Hill set everything in motion.”

That momentum eventually led to an introduction from Wayne Wonder, which opened doors to King Promotions, touring opportunities with producer and songwriter Jazze Pha and, in 2023, performing before an audience of over 60,000 people during hip hop’s 50th anniversary celebration.

“It was electrifying. There’s really no other word to describe it. To me, standing on one of hip hop’s greatest stages, surrounded by some of the biggest names in the culture, celebrating 50 years of a genre that was born from Jamaican sound system culture, as a Jamaican DJ was priceless,” he said. “Every obstacle, every sacrifice, every door that was closed before one finally opened, all of it flashed in that moment. Not many DJs will ever have that experience. And standing there, I knew without a doubt that it was exactly where I was supposed to be. That feeling is truly indescribable.”

DJ Damage hopes his story encourages the next generation of creatives to dream bigger than their circumstances.

“These are moments I worked for over 20 years. I started with nothing but a chance and a will to prove myself. I hope young creatives across Jamaica and the Caribbean will see this win and know that if they have a dream and don’t know if it’s possible, it is.”

Following his latest achievements, DJ Damage will continue his momentum with a performance at the 41st Annual Stellar Gospel Music Awards on August 15 at the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. The awards ceremony will be later aired on BET.

World.title: Wellington praises Team Jamaica after World U-20 exploits
World.content:
Shanoya Douglas won three medals for Jamaica — gold in the women’s 4x100m relay and silver in the 100m and 200m. (Photo: Paul Reid)

OREGON, USA — Keith Wellington, team leader for Jamaica at the 21st staging of the World Athletics Under-20 Championships, says the team performed well despite the challenges of a long season.

Jamaica won eight medals — two gold, three silver and three bronze — to finish fourth on the medal table and third in the placing table with 89 points.

Hosts United States topped both tables with 24 medals —12 gold, seven silver and five bronze. Kenya were second with 11 medals — four gold, three silver and four bronze — while Italy finished third with five medals — three gold and two bronze.

Shanoya Douglas was Jamaica’s most successful athlete, winning three medals — gold in the women’s 4x100m relay and silver in the 100m and 200m.

Wellington said the performances were particularly impressive given that most of the athletes had been competing since January.

“I think under any circumstances this would be a really good performance,” Wellington told the Jamaica Observer on Sunday before the final two relays were contested. “Eight medals to date, and third in terms of quality.”

He said the overall standard at the championships had improved significantly.

“We have seen some really world-class standards, not just as juniors but the quality of the performances has been really, really good overall for all the countries. And so, to still be amongst the best, I think, we would be proud of the performances.”

Wellington singled out Michael Andre Edwards’ dramatic victory in the men’s triple jump during which he produced a World Under-20-leading and personal best 17.08m — the fifth-longest winning mark in the history of the event at the championships.

“Yeah, I think the obvious standout would be Team Captain Michael Andre’s performance. Not just the 17.08m but remember, you know, he took the lead with his second-to-last jump. It was taken away from him and he came back and claimed it. So it’s not just the result, but the quality and the performance there.”

He also highlighted the men’s discus throw competition on Sunday involving Jamaicans Joseph Salmon and Kamari Kennedy, when the lead changed several times over the final two rounds.

Jamaica also set two national records in the mixed 4x100m relay, which was contested for the first time at the championships, and the mixed 4x400m relay.

Ten Jamaicans produced personal bests, including Shevaughn Thomas and Sashane Johnson who each recorded two personal best performances.

Wellington said the athletes’ performances should not be judged solely by their results, pointing to the demands of the Jamaican school season.

“I think we don’t want to just look at the results, but look at the performances and you can see quite a few quality performances. And we cannot ignore, again, that our juniors have a really long season; and it is the schools that invest most in these kids, so they have to peak for champs because that is where the investment is,” he said.

“And so, for them to come back five months after their last performance for their schools again is sometimes a challenge that many of them have exams in the middle and all of that. So, I think it’s an incredible performance.”

World.title: STAYING PUT!
World.content:
Sanjay Seymore (left) anchors Jamaica’s men’s 4x100m relay team to victory in the semi-finals of the World Athletics Under-20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon, on Saturday. Jamaica ran 39.51 seconds to advance to the final. At centre is Hong Kong’s Cheuk Fung Jasper Koo, while at right is Australia’s Joshua John. (Photo: Paul A Reid)

OREGON, USA — William Knibb Memorial High School’s Sanjay Seymore has turned down several offers from United States colleges, choosing to remain in Jamaica as he targets places on the country’s teams for the 2027 World Athletics Championships and 2028 Olympic Games.

The ISSA/GraceKennedy Boys’ and Girls’ Athletics Championships and Carifta Games 200m champion is coming off a season of highs and lows, including finishing third in his favourite event at the Jamaica Athletics Administrative Association (JAAA) National Junior Championships and missing out on an individual spot on Jamaica’s team to the 21st World Athletics Under-20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon.

Seymore, who recently signed a professional contract, declined to give details about his plans but confirmed to the Jamaica Observer on Sunday that he would remain in Jamaica for now.

“I can say definitely I’m staying in Jamaica for now. So yes, that’s the only thing I can say right now that I would be staying in Jamaica.”

He said he believes remaining at home gives him the best opportunity to make Jamaica’s teams for the World Championships and Olympics.

“It’s just I think it’s the best for me right now, I don’t really have anything against college,” he said. “I see that when you go college and then come back for the Jamaica trials, athletes are not at their best and then and you know we have World Championship and Olympics coming up.”

At 19, Seymore believes he has time to develop as he prepares to compete against some of the world’s leading sprinters, including Jamaica’s Oblique Seville.

“They already have their reputations, Oblique Seville is a world champion, so you can’t take that from him. So, as the rookie, I would say I’m just going into the big game with the seniors, and I’m just going to give it my best shot always, like I done in junior levels. But I know I have to put the best foot forward if I want to make it big as a Jamaican sprinter. So that’s definitely goal for me.”

Seymore had been expected to qualify for Jamaica’s team in the 200m but suffered an injury shortly before the JAAA Championships. He finished third in the final in 21.01 seconds behind Nathaniel Martin and Kyle Bodden.

He was subsequently added to the men’s 4x100m relay team and ran two strong anchor legs as Jamaica won bronze.

“After Carifta I had some injuries, went to trials and came third as I was coming back from the injury,” he said. “But I got my mind right and told myself I’m going to go on this relay and I’m going to give it my best shot and go into the best possible shape I can for the team.”

Seymore said he was pleased with his contribution to the bronze-medal effort.

“So I just went out there and give my best and we came short of the gold medal, but we still made the podium, so I’m pretty happy for that.”

World.title: BWE organisers respond to viral fight video, reaffirms commitment to patron safety
World.content:
Videograb showing a brawl at a Best Weekend Ever beach event on Sunday, August 10, 2026.

ST ANN, Jamaica – The directors of party series Best Weekend Ever (BWE) has expressed disappointment and regret over a physical altercation involving patrons at its beach event on Sunday.

Videos of the incident have been widely circulated on social media, showing a group of men engaged in a brawl.

In a media release Monday, the party organisers said, “Best Weekend Ever has never condoned, and we abhor the proliferation of violence of any kind at our events.

“We are extremely disappointed and sincerely regret that this unfortunate and isolated situation has occurred,” the release continued. “We have contacted the family of those affected and the individuals involved in the altercation have been clearly identified, and the relevant actions will be pursued by the designated authority.”

According to the directors, over the years, BWE has established a strong track record of providing safe, well-managed entertainment experiences for thousands of patrons.

“The safety and security of our guests remain a priority, and this incident is not reflective of the culture of Best Weekend Ever or the experience we work diligently to provide,” they said.

The directors also sought to clarify that, contrary to some narratives circulating, the MC at the event “brought attention to the incident to allow the appropriate intervention to take place and we have made our team available to the relevant authorities to assist in the process of ensuring this does not reoccur.”

According to the release, throughout the staging of Best Weekend Ever 2026, the events have been enjoyed safely by thousands of patrons with improved traffic management and movement between events.

“We are also grateful for the positive feedback from patrons which is an indication of the high level of satisfaction with the production of the event series,” the organisers said.

“Additional security measures have been put in place for the final event being staged today,” they added. “We thank our patrons, partners, security teams and stakeholders for their support as we continue to remain committed to delivering an environment where everyone can celebrate responsibly and safely.”

World.title: Tropical depression could form in Atlantic by the end of the week
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — The United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is advising that a tropical depression could form in the Atlantic during the latter half of this week.

The NOAA says an area of low pressure located a few hundred miles south of the Cabo Verde Islands is producing disorganised showers and thunderstorms.

As this system moves slowly westward, a tropical wave currently over west Africa is expected to merge with it in a couple of days.

Environmental conditions are forecast to be more conducive for development by midweek, and a tropical depression could form during the latter half of this week while the system moves westward to west-northwestward across the central tropical Atlantic.

Formation chance through 48 hours is low at 20 per cent but formation chance through seven days is medium at 60 per cent.

World.title: Bold Bruce
World.content:
Former Prime Minister Bruce Golding

NEW YORK, USA — Former Jamaican Prime Minister Bruce Golding has earned the backing of many within the Diaspora community here for what is being described as his “bold, factual and truthful position” on the souring relationship between Jamaica and America, two staunch allies.



Speaking in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania last week, Golding expressed hopes that “the United States will soften the tone of its relationship with Jamaica and rekindle the strong, decades-old bond between both nations which Jamaicans cherish.

Saying that current demands by Washington are “at odds with the very essence of true friendship”, he pointed to the many challenges facing the island as established rules are being discarded and “new rules are being handed down, not after discussions and negotiations, but unilaterally by social media postings at 2:30 in the morning when most of us are asleep”.

The former Jamaican leader, who stepped away in 2011 and handed over the reins to now Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness, was addressing the annual Team Jamaica Bickle Independence Gala on Emancipation Day, August 1, 2026.

The gala celebrated Jamaica’s 64th anniversary of Independence and raised funds in support of Jamaican and other Caribbean athletes’ participation in the yearly Penn Relays in the US, a must-stop on the annual sports calendar for speedy Jamaican high school students.

Golding appeared to be voicing sentiments many Jamaicans in his US audience feel but could not express themselves. Some murmured among themselves that he must not fear losing his US visa.

Called to ask his view Sunday, Golding said he did not wish to trivialise the matter and he had said enough on the subject.

But reacting to the former prime minister’s assessment of the bilateral relations, Stafford Grant, founder and president of the US-based Jamaica Ex-Service Men and Women Foundation, said after the speech:

“Golding didn’t just give a speech, he gave Jamaica a masterclass in geopolitical survival. His address laid bare the brutal reality of being a small island nation caught in the cross hairs of superpower diplomacy.

“The former prime minister’s speech should serve as a profound wake-up call for every Jamaican. His vocal defence is more critical than ever, and I trust Jamaicans will understand that international diplomacy is shifting from collaborative negotiations to unilateral madness,” Grant declared.

Raymond Rhoden, a Florida-based retired adjunct professor, described Golding’s stance as “bold, principled, factual and diplomatic”, adding that he believes Jamaica needs to stand up and take a principled position on the current situation.

Irwine Clare Sr, co-founder of Team Jamaica Bickle, said the issues raised by the former head of government were “pungent, timely, and well articulated on behalf of the voiceless and those who have avoided the conversation due to fear of reprisal or just being downright spineless”.

“This speech must also be placed in context, because clearly he [Golding] recognises the agonising situation that Caribbean leaders find themselves in, especially against the backdrop that they do not speak from a united perspective,” said Clare Sr.

In his address, which was punctuated by applause, Golding spoke of the discontinuation of the Cuban medical mission programme, America’s fierce opposition to China’s investments in Jamaica, and the highly controversial third-country nationals arrangements between the US and a number of Caribbean countries, as examples of actions that run counter to harmonious relations.

“True friends don’t abuse your friendship; they don’t make unreasonable demands of you. They should be there to help you. Holding a gun at your head and insisting that you must be reasonable and do things their way is not friendship,” Golding suggested.

“The United States has put us under severe stress, and that’s not what friends are for,” he said, pointing to the damage the Jamaican economy could suffer should Jamaica stand up and try to fight back.

“There are many at home and abroad who are outraged at what is taking place, who are incensed at what is being meted out to us, who are angry that we have not pushed back, that we haven’t stood up like President Lula da Silva of Brazil who declared that, ‘Brazil’s destiny is for Brazilians alone to determine — without foreign interference or otherwise.’ “

Noting that Brazil is large and provides a US$57-billion market for American exports, Golding warned that little Jamaica is not in that league, struggling to find markets for its own goods.

“With the US market accounting for half our total exports, if our exports to the US market were slapped with a 50 per cent tariff our manufacturing sector would fall apart and thousands of persons would lose their jobs,” said Golding.

Agreeing with Golding, Dr Rupert Francis, who heads the Jamaica Diaspora Task Force on Crime Intervention and Prevention, argued that “we need to get back to the more amiable friendship we had with the United States for many years”.

University lecturer Dr Allan Cunningham said Golding’s speech focused on what he describes as the “hypocrisy of the rules-based order”, noting that “the speech acts as a call for regional realism — that without a unified foreign policy Caribbean states remain vulnerable to US cowboy diplomacy”.

World.title: Latvia discovers secret migrant tunnel at Belarus frontier
World.content:
Tunnels have previously been found in Lithuania, according to Baltic media, but this is the first time one has been used to cross into Latvia.

“This is the first case in which a tunnel has been used for illegal crossing of the state border into Latvia. No signs of violations had previously been detected in this exact location, and no detentions of persons illegally crossing the state border had occurred there,” Dombrava wrote on X.

Authorities returned all 15 people to their “country of departure” and are continuing to inspect the area around the tunnel.

Latvia launched an operation Tuesday to strengthen border security. Dombrava has described illegal border crossings from Belarus as a “hybrid threat.”

Authorities have prevented more than 9,000 illegal attempts to cross the border from Belarus so far this year, the Latvian State Border Guard said in a press release.

World.title: Putin used North Korean ballistic missiles in lethal attack on Ukraine, Zelenskyy says
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean ruler Kim Jong Un have deepened ties since the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine began. In September last year during a meeting in Beijing, Kim vowed to do “everything we can to assist Russia.”

Zelenskyy also reported attacks on a Kyiv hospital and businesses overnight, with at least one person injured. The capital’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, urged residents late Monday to seek shelter.

Moscow also attacked substations in Kherson and Kharkiv, causing power outages, Zelenskyy said. Further attacks took place in the Donetsk, Dnipro and Mykolaiv regions.

“Every step Russia takes — increasing ballistic missile production, bringing in North Korean equipment, preparing for mobilization — all of this shows that Moscow is preparing not for peace, but for escalation,” Zelenskyy wrote.

Russia has stepped up its missile attacks this summer, with Zelenskyy urging Western allies to help Kyiv strengthen its air defenses and to heap sanctions pressure on companies fueling Moscow’s war. However, Europe is running out of Patriot interceptors to shoot down Russian missiles, according to the continent’s military officials.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has struck back, targeting Russian infrastructure including oil refineries and buildings belonging to e-commerce giant Wildberries.

Russian state media on Tuesday reported that two Wildberries warehouses in the Voronezh region, several hundred kilometers south of Moscow, caught fire following drone strikes, killing one person.

World.title: Trump backs Infantino after fury over FIFA chief’s World Cup sale plan
World.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino stands beside U.S. President Donald Trump with the World Cup trophy before presenting it to Spain after the final at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026. | Dan Mullan/Getty Images

It would be a “terrible mistake” to replace the football boss after the success of the 2026 World Cup, the U.S. president posted on Truth Social.

U.S. President Donald Trump backed under-pressure football chief Gianni Infantino, after calls grew for the FIFA boss to quit following his aborted plan to sell off parts of the World Cup tournament to private investors.

“FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino. He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented,” Trump posted Tuesday morning on Truth Social.

Trump and Infantino cultivated a close relationship in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup, hosted this summer in North America, and the U.S. president helped present the trophy to victorious Spain in New Jersey in July.
